校正前有五个变量达到名义显着性(两个 CD8 + T 细胞亚群以及 IL-1β、IL-10 和 MIP-1α),但校正后没有一个变量保持显着性。在先天免疫群体中没有观察到任何变化,也没有检测到残留的证据。 [10.14814/phy2.71031]
该研究在健康样本对比中,识别出65个在严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2两种变异株中显著差异表达的miRNA,并观察到特定miRNA表达与患者症状严重程度之间存在关联。 [10.1007/s11033-026-12632-x]
相当比例的 TCR 针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 的表位,包括非结构蛋白;分析提示炎症小体活性下降和单核细胞分化受损,表明可能存在免疫耗竭或未成熟。 [10.3389/fimmu.2026.1937175]
已对图表及源数据进行更正,以消除重复值,确保HTML和PDF版本中的数据准确性。 [10.1038/s41467-026-77179-8]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: At Day 8, CD4+ T cells (Th1 profile) increased in all study groups, while CD8+ T cells increased in all groups except the lowest CV0701 dose group. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases were reported. [10.1080/21645515.2026.2715900]
COVID-19 thrombi showed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance and diffuse CD68+ staining, reduced platelet content, and a disorganized fibrillar network. [10.1007/s00401-026-03074-7]

Five variables reached nominal significance before correction (two CD8 + T‐cell subsets and IL‐1β, IL‐10, and MIP‐1α), but none remained significant after adjustment. No changes were observed in innate immune populations, and no evidence of carryover was detected. [10.14814/phy2.71031]

The study identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples, and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity in patients. [10.1007/s11033-026-12632-x]

A significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins, and the analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation, indicating potential immune exhaustion or immaturity. [10.3389/fimmu.2026.1937175]

news.headline_zh: SARS-CoV-2本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期SARS-CoV-2新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: CDC发布了一份关于呼吸道病毒活动水平的报告,其中包含与大肠杆菌、沙门氏菌等多种病原体相关的暴发的信息,以及埃博拉和环孢子虫病的最新情况。该报告是一份公共卫生主题的总体概述,并未重点关注某一特定暴发或病毒。 [news-31e57dad649983cf]

A two-year study tracked cognitive changes in patients hospitalized with COVID-19 during the Omicron-dominant period, finding that most patients recovered, while some experienced persistent or progressive cognitive decline. [news-6f31992e117d85cc]
A comprehensive pediatric study, the Pediatric COVID Outcomes Study (PECOS), was conducted to examine the long-term effects of COVID-19 on children. [news-0a1136272324c9ad]

Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health's IVAC researchers contributed to the World Health Organization's (WHO) first-ever position paper on COVID-19 vaccines, which summarizes vaccine performance and safety data. [news-7c036cfba5b3ccae]

The article discusses the emergence of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, and its global impact. It is confirmed as the cause of the pandemic, with evidence of its transmission and symptoms. [news-5578de946ea7d789]

papers.title: Safety and immunogenicity of an mRNA COVID-19 vaccine administered to adults: A phase 2, randomized, active-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: We conducted a phase 2, randomized, active-controlled, observer-blind study (NCT05960097) among healthy adults ≥18 y of age who completed a primary COVID-19 mRNA vaccination series, with or without a booster, ≥3 months earlier. Participants were randomized (1:1:1:1:1) to either receive an investigational bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine encoding ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 spike proteins (CV0701 mRNA vaccine) at one of three dose levels, an investigational monovalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine encoding the Omicron BA.4-5 spike protein (CV0601 mRNA vaccine), or a licensed Original Wuhan/Omicron BA.4-5 bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccine. The primary objectives were to evaluate reactogenicity, safety and immunogenicity post-vaccination. Secondary and tertiary objectives were to further evaluate humoral and cell-mediated immunity post-vaccination. In total, 425 participants were vaccinated and 381 were included in the Day 29 per-protocol immunogenicity analysis. Most solicited events were mild to moderate. No vaccine-related serious adverse events or myocarditis/pericarditis cases were reported. For the CV0701 mRNA vaccine, a dose-dependent increase in Day 29 neutralizing titers against ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 was observed. Neutralizing titers against ancestral D614G and Omicron BA.4-5 declined by Days 91 and 181, but remained above baseline. Similar immune responses were observed for the CV0601 mRNA vaccine. At Day 8, CD4+ T cells (Th1 profile) increased in all study groups and CD8+ T cells increased in all study groups, except the lowest CV0701 dose group. The CV0701 and CV0601 mRNA vaccines elicited robust humoral and cellular immunity with an acceptable safety profile, comparable to a licensed, bivalent mRNA vaccine. Clinical Trial Registration EU CT number: 2023-504596-25-00 ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05960097.

papers.title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
papers.abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in 70.2% (33/47) of immunocompromised patients with mAb-resistant infections, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term outcomes, durability of viral clearance, or comparative efficacy against newer antiviral agents. Additionally, the small sample size (47 cases) and reliance on unpublished cases limit generalizability and robustness of conclusions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for randomized controlled trials to validate CCP efficacy in immunocompromised populations and to determine optimal dosing strategies. Surveillance for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants resistant to both mAbs and CCP is recommended to guide treatment protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes correlating with improved outcomes. The review underscores CCP's potential role in overcoming mAb resistance but emphasizes the need for larger, controlled studies to confirm efficacy, optimize dosing, and assess long-term durability. Given the limited sample size and reliance on unpublished data, findings should be interpreted cautiously.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in 70.2% (33/47) of immunocompromised patients with mAb-resistant infections, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. Total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with viral clearance in logistic regression analysis.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report long-term outcomes, durability of viral clearance, or comparative efficacy against newer antiviral agents. Additionally, the small sample size (47 cases) and reliance on unpublished cases limit generalizability and robustness of conclusions.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for randomized controlled trials to validate CCP efficacy in immunocompromised populations and to determine optimal dosing strategies. Surveillance for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants resistant to both mAbs and CCP is recommended to guide treatment protocols.

papers.title_zh: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
papers.source_body_en: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.

papers.title: Immunological effects of supervised exercise in long COVID in adults: A secondary analysis of a randomized crossover trial
papers.abstract: Abstract Long COVID (post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection) affects approximately 5%–30% of survivors and is characterized by persistent fatigue, dyspnea, exercise intolerance, and cognitive impairment. We evaluated the immunological effects of supervised exercise in adults with long COVID. In this pre‐specified exploratory substudy of the EXER‐COVID randomized 2 × 2 crossover trial, participants completed a 6‐week supervised exercise program (twice weekly) or usual care before crossing over after a 3–5 day washout. Plasma cytokines (IL‐1β, IL‐6, IL‐10, TNF‐α, MCP‐1/CCL2, MIP‐1α/CCL3, MIP‐1β/CCL4, and IP‐10/CXCL10) were measured by multiplex immunoassay. Immunophenotyping included 20 CD4 + and CD8 + T‐cell subsets and five innate immune populations. Treatment effects were estimated using within‐period change scores, with multiple testing controlled by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure (false discovery rate < 5%). Five variables reached nominal significance before correction (two CD8 + T‐cell subsets and IL‐1β, IL‐10, and MIP‐1α), but none remained significant after adjustment. No changes were observed in innate immune populations, and no evidence of carryover was detected. Supervised exercise was not associated with significant immunological changes after correction for multiple comparisons, supporting the short‐term immunological safety of moderate‐intensity exercise in PESE‐negative adults with long COVID ( ClinicalTrials.gov : NCT04797871).

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 长新冠(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的急性后遗症)影响大约 5%–30% 的幸存者,其特点是持续疲劳、呼吸困难、运动不耐受和认知障碍。我们评估了 长新冠 成人监督运动的免疫学效果。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 EXER-COVID 随机 2 × 2 交叉试验的这项预先指定的探索性子研究中,参与者在 3-5 天的冲洗后完成了为期 6 周的监督锻炼计划(每周两次)或常规护理,然后再进行常规护理。免疫表型分析包括 20 个 CD4 + 和 CD8 + T 细胞亚群以及 5 个先天免疫群体。
elements_zh.methods: 通过多重免疫分析测定血浆细胞因子(IL-1β、IL-6、IL-10、TNF-α、MCP-1/CCL2、MIP-1α/CCL3、MIP-1β/CCL4 和 IP-10/CXCL10)。治疗 效应使用期间变化评分进行估计,并通过 Benjamini-Hochberg 程序控制多重测试(错误发现率 < 5%)。
elements_zh.main_results: 校正前有五个变量达到名义显着性(两个 CD8 + T 细胞亚群以及 IL-1β、IL-10 和 MIP-1α),但校正后没有一个变量保持显着性。在先天免疫群体中没有观察到任何变化,也没有检测到残留的证据。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 经过多重比较校正后,监督运动与显着的免疫学变化无关,支持 PESE 阴性 长新冠 成人中等强度运动的短期免疫安全性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,监督运动可能是成人 长新冠 患者的一种安全干预措施,可能为未来针对这种疾病的治疗方法的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是对随机交叉试验的二次分析,并对结果进行了多重比较调整。由于分析的探索性和潜在的混杂因素,证据的强度适中。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 长新冠(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的急性后遗症)影响大约 5%–30% 的幸存者,其特点是持续疲劳、呼吸困难、运动不耐受和认知障碍。我们评估了 长新冠 成人监督运动的免疫学效果。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 在 EXER-COVID 随机 2 × 2 交叉试验的这项预先指定的探索性子研究中,参与者在 3-5 天的冲洗后完成了为期 6 周的监督锻炼计划(每周两次)或常规护理,然后再进行常规护理。免疫表型分析包括 20 个 CD4 + 和 CD8 + T 细胞亚群以及 5 个先天免疫群体。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过多重免疫分析测定血浆细胞因子(IL-1β、IL-6、IL-10、TNF-α、MCP-1/CCL2、MIP-1α/CCL3、MIP-1β/CCL4 和 IP-10/CXCL10)。治疗 效应使用期间变化评分进行估计,并通过 Benjamini-Hochberg 程序控制多重测试(错误发现率 < 5%)。
analysis_zh.main_results: 校正前有五个变量达到名义显着性(两个 CD8 + T 细胞亚群以及 IL-1β、IL-10 和 MIP-1α),但校正后没有一个变量保持显着性。在先天免疫群体中没有观察到任何变化,也没有检测到残留的证据。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 经过多重比较校正后,监督运动与显着的免疫学变化无关,支持 PESE 阴性 长新冠 成人中等强度运动的短期免疫安全性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,监督运动可能是成人 长新冠 患者的一种安全干预措施,可能为未来针对这种疾病的治疗方法的研究提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是对随机交叉试验的二次分析,并对结果进行了多重比较调整。由于分析的探索性和潜在的混杂因素,证据的强度适中。

papers.title: Psychoeducational Challenges of Dyslexic Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Dyslexic students faced psychological and educational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and online learning, including increased anxiety, low self-esteem, reduced reading interest, limited access to educational technologies, insufficient teacher support, and difficulties with reading fluency and concentration. Examining these challenges is crucial for implementing effective measures and enhancing post-pandemic learning. This study investigates the psycho-educational challenges of dyslexic children during the pandemic, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to support them in current and future contexts. This systematic review identified relevant articles through electronic searches of PubMed, Wiley, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by the snowballing technique, which involved examining the bibliographies of retrieved references. The study identified two main categories of challenges for dyslexic children: psychological (mental health, emotional well-being, behavioural issues, parental stress) and educational (socioeconomic status, technology access, special educational needs, teacher support, remote learning difficulties) affecting children with learning disabilities. The research results show that dyslexic children faced various psychological and educational difficulties identified in this review during the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, targeted, evidence-based strategies-such as teacher training, family-school collaboration, adaptive learning technologies, and psychological support-are needed to mitigate these challenges in the post-pandemic period.

papers.title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.
papers.abstract: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use. We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study. PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through May 2026. Thirty-one studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) were included. The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response. Among RCTs analysing timing, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration; for titre, 3 of 4 RCTs with explicit comparisons found benefit with higher-titre CP; and two large RCTs (combined n = 12,522) demonstrated preferential benefit in seronegative recipients. This interpretation is consistent with modelling estimates that CP, deployed largely to hospitalised patients, nonetheless saved tens of thousands of lives in the United States during the first pandemic year, an effect attributed to the subset treated early enough to modify disease progression. A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment. These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) for COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2, focusing on three interacting determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics, to reconcile conflicting trial outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM) was conducted, searching PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus through May 2026, applying a standardized 91-field extraction matrix to 31 included studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CP is effective only under specific conditions: early administration, sufficient antibody titre, and in seronegative or immunocompromised hosts lacking endogenous antibody responses. Among RCTs, 4 of 6 found benefit with earlier administration, 3 of 4 with higher-titre CP, and two large RCTs (n=12,522) showed preferential benefit in seronegative recipients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM) in CP products is nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies reporting such data despite evidence of their potent neutralising activity against SARS-CoV-2, representing a systematic gap in product assessment.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritise standardised quantification of IgA/IgM titres in CP products and evaluate precision deployment strategies for passive immunotherapy in future pandemics, leveraging timing and titre determinants to optimise efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review resolves conflicting evidence on convalescent plasma (CP) efficacy in COVID-19 by identifying three critical determinants: early administration, high antibody titre, and host seronegativity or immunocompromise. Among 31 studies (20,793 patients), randomized trials showed benefit when CP was given early (4/6 trials) or with higher titres (3/4 trials), particularly in seronegative recipients (two large RCTs, n=12,522). However, a major evidence gap persists: only 2 studies assessed non-IgG immunoglobulins (IgA/IgM), despite their potential potency. The review reframes CP efficacy as conditional and provides a template for precision deployment in future pandemics, emphasizing the need for standardized IgA/IgM quantification and targeted clinical strategies.

papers.title: High levels of cell-free hemoglobin and iron in cerebral thrombi of pre-Omicron COVID-19 stroke patients: novel drivers of SARS-CoV-2–induced prothrombotic state
papers.abstract: The pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events associated with COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. To investigate prothrombotic alterations during SARS-CoV-2 infection, we performed an exploratory and integrated analysis of cerebral thrombi retrieved, during the first wave of the pandemic, by mechanical thrombectomy from stroke patients with (n=6) and without (n=6) COVID-19. We combined histological and ultrastructural assessment with quantitative proteomics and elemental profiling to identify differences in cellular organization and in protein and metal composition. Immunohistochemical quantification revealed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance, a more diffuse CD68+ staining pattern, and reduced platelet content in COVID-19 thrombi. In contrast, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) burden, neutrophil number, and erythrocyte content did not differ significantly between groups. Transmission electron microscopy showed a disorganized ultrastructural fibrillar network in thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients, consistent with the irregular and less densely packed extracellular matrix observed by Masson's trichrome staining. Furthermore, quantitative proteomics by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with marked upregulation of hemoglobin subunits (α, β, γ, and δ), haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase and redox-regulating proteins, alongside downregulation of platelet-related proteins in COVID-19 thrombi. Total reflection X-ray fluorescence (TXRF) confirmed increased iron levels in COVID-19-associated thrombi. Notably, glycophorin A immunostaining did not indicate increased erythrocyte abundance, and erythrocyte structural proteins were not differentially expressed in proteomic analysis, suggesting that hemoglobin and iron were largely present in a cell-free form within the retrieved thrombi of COVID-19 stroke patients. In addition, acute-phase reactants, classical complement components, and immunoglobulins were detected exclusively in COVID-19 samples, consistent with a distinctive immune-inflammatory and oxidative signature. Overall, these findings support a novel pathophysiological mechanism underlying COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability and thrombosis, involving elevated circulating cell-free hemoglobin and increased iron content. Furthermore, this study highlights the potential contribution of hemoglobin/iron-related processes to the COVID-19 prothrombotic state and may provide molecular targets for future therapeutic strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the incomplete understanding of mechanisms driving the hypercoagulable state and thrombotic events in COVID-19, aiming to identify novel prothrombotic alterations associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An exploratory, integrated analysis was conducted on cerebral thrombi retrieved by mechanical thrombectomy from six stroke patients with COVID-19 and six without COVID-19 during the first pandemic wave.
analysis.methods: Histological and ultrastructural assessments were combined with quantitative proteomics (LC–MS/MS) and elemental profiling (TXRF) to compare cellular organization, protein composition, and metal content between thrombi from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients.
analysis.main_results: COVID-19 thrombi showed a trend toward increased macrophage abundance and diffuse CD68+ staining, reduced platelet content, and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics identified 48 differentially expressed proteins among 720 shared proteins, with upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, biliverdin reductase, and redox-regulating proteins, and downregulation of platelet-related proteins. TXRF confirmed increased iron levels, while glycophorin A immunostaining and erythrocyte structural proteins indicated cell-free hemoglobin and iron presence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as supporting a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability involving elevated cell-free hemoglobin and iron, distinct from NETs burden or erythrocyte abundance. They highlight the identification of hemoglobin/iron-related processes as a potential molecular target for future therapies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that hemoglobin and iron dysregulation may contribute to the prothrombotic state in COVID-19, potentially informing diagnostic or therapeutic strategies targeting these pathways in stroke patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=6 per group) and exploratory design limit generalizability and causal inference. The study relies on thrombi retrieved during a specific pandemic wave, which may not represent later variants or broader populations, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This exploratory study investigated prothrombotic alterations in cerebral thrombi from COVID-19 stroke patients compared to non-COVID-19 controls during the first pandemic wave. Using histological, ultrastructural, proteomic, and elemental analyses, the authors identified increased cell-free hemoglobin and iron levels in COVID-19 thrombi, alongside reduced platelet content and a disorganized fibrillar network. Proteomics revealed upregulation of hemoglobin subunits, haptoglobin, and redox-regulating proteins, with downregulation of platelet-related proteins. These findings support a novel mechanism for COVID-19-associated hypercoagulability distinct from NETs or erythrocyte abundance. While the study provides mechanistic insights, its small sample size and focus on early pandemic thrombi limit generalizability and preclude causal conclusions.

papers.title: Engineering antigenic breadth against SARS-CoV-2 by pairing divergent RBDs within a single mRNA immunogen.
papers.abstract: Vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal for pandemic preparedness. A challenge across vaccine fields is how to deliberately recruit the rare B cell clones that recognize conserved epitopes shared across diverse viral variants. BnAbs have been known to frequently emerge through extensive somatic hypermutation during affinity maturation, here we describe an alternative mechanism for bnAb selection. We designed an mRNA vaccine in which two antigenically distinct (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) SARS-CoV-2 variant's (Omicron and Delta; O-Δ) receptor binding domains (RBDs) are physically fused on a single polypeptide. This design is predicted to favor B cell antigen receptors capable of engaging conserved epitopes on both RBDs with enhanced avidity. A matched nondivergent tandem RBD (Delta-Delta; Δ-Δ) served as a control. In mice, immunization elicited potent antibody responses and increased the frequency of cross-reactive B cells, recognizing Delta, Omicron, and the 2002 pandemic strain SARS-CoV RBDs. Using multicolor RBD tetramers and single-cell B cell receptor sequencing, we show that breadth arises via two distinct pathways. The divergent vaccine preferentially enriches clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells (not present within non-cross-reactive B cell pools) with low levels of somatic hypermutation, consistent with selection of germline-biased precursors. In contrast, the matched control vaccine yields cross-reactivity primarily within existing clonal lineages (clonal overlap between cross-reactive and non-cross-reactive cells) and at higher mutational burdens, consistent with affinity-maturation-driven acquisition of breadth. This work establishes a simple, modular antigen-design principle in which juxtaposing appropriately divergent antigens on a single scaffold promotes the enrichment of bnAb-prone B cells.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal for pandemic preparedness, yet a challenge across vaccine fields is how to deliberately recruit the rare B cell clones that recognize conserved epitopes shared across diverse viral variants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study designed an mRNA vaccine in which two antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variant receptor binding domains (Omicron and Delta) are physically fused on a single polypeptide, with a matched nondivergent tandem RBD (Delta-Delta) serving as a control.
analysis.methods: Using multicolor RBD tetramers and single-cell B cell receptor sequencing, the authors assessed B cell receptor selection and cross-reactivity pathways induced by the divergent and matched control vaccines.
analysis.main_results: In mice, immunization with the divergent vaccine elicited potent antibody responses and increased the frequency of cross-reactive B cells recognizing Delta, Omicron, and the 2002 pandemic strain SARS-CoV RBDs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The divergent vaccine preferentially enriches clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells with low somatic hypermutation, consistent with selection of germline-biased precursors, whereas the matched control yields cross-reactivity primarily through affinity maturation within existing clonal lineages.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This work establishes a modular antigen-design principle in which juxtaposing appropriately divergent antigens on a single scaffold promotes the enrichment of bnAb-prone B cells, offering a strategy for broader vaccine coverage against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to preclinical mouse data and does not report human immunogenicity, durability of responses, or clinical efficacy, warranting cautious interpretation of translational potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the need for vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) against diverse SARS-CoV-2 variants by designing an mRNA immunogen that pairs divergent receptor binding domains (RBDs) from Omicron and Delta on a single polypeptide. In mice, the divergent vaccine elicited potent antibody responses and increased cross-reactive B cell frequencies against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the 2002 SARS-CoV strain. Mechanistically, breadth arose via two pathways: the divergent vaccine enriched germline-biased, clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells with low somatic hypermutation, while the matched control vaccine induced cross-reactivity primarily through affinity maturation within existing clonal lineages. The authors propose a modular antigen-design principle to deliberately recruit bnAb-prone B cells, offering a potential strategy for broader vaccine coverage. However, the evidence is preclinical and limited to mouse models, leaving human immunogenicity, durability, and clinical efficacy unassessed.

papers.title_zh: 通过在单一mRNA免疫原中配对发散受体结合域以增强对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的抗原性广度
papers.source_body_en: Vaccines capable of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are a major goal for pandemic preparedness. A challenge across vaccine fields is how to deliberately recruit the rare B cell clones that recognize conserved epitopes shared across diverse viral variants. BnAbs have been known to frequently emerge through extensive somatic hypermutation during affinity maturation, here we describe an alternative mechanism for bnAb selection. We designed an mRNA vaccine in which two antigenically distinct (severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2) SARS-CoV-2 variant's (Omicron and Delta; O-Δ) receptor binding domains (RBDs) are physically fused on a single polypeptide. This design is predicted to favor B cell antigen receptors capable of engaging conserved epitopes on both RBDs with enhanced avidity. A matched nondivergent tandem RBD (Delta-Delta; Δ-Δ) served as a control. In mice, immunization elicited potent antibody responses and increased the frequency of cross-reactive B cells, recognizing Delta, Omicron, and the 2002 pandemic strain SARS-CoV RBDs. Using multicolor RBD tetramers and single-cell B cell receptor sequencing, we show that breadth arises via two distinct pathways. The divergent vaccine preferentially enriches clonally distinct cross-reactive B cells (not present within non-cross-reactive B cell pools) with low levels of somatic hypermutation, consistent with selection of germline-biased precursors. In contrast, the matched control vaccine yields cross-reactivity primarily within existing clonal lineages (clonal overlap between cross-reactive and non-cross-reactive cells) and at higher mutational burdens, consistent with affinity-maturation-driven acquisition of breadth. This work establishes a simple, modular antigen-design principle in which juxtaposing appropriately divergent antigens on a single scaffold promotes the enrichment of bnAb-prone B cells.
papers.abstract_zh: 能够诱导广泛中和抗体(bnAbs)的疫苗是疫情防控的重要目标。然而,在疫苗领域,如何有意识地招募识别不同病毒变异株间保守表位的罕见B细胞克隆仍是一大挑战。已知bnAbs通常通过亲和力成熟过程中的大量体细胞超突变产生,而本研究描述了一种bnAb选择的替代机制。我们设计了一种mRNA 疫苗,其中两个抗原性不同的(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2)严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变异株(Omicron和Delta;O-Δ)的受体结合域(RBD)在单一多肽链上进行物理融合。该设计预计可增强能够同时结合两个RBD上保守表位的B细胞抗原受体的亲和力。匹配的非发散串联RBD(Delta-Delta;Δ-Δ)作为对照。在小鼠中,免疫接种诱导了强效抗体应答并提高了交叉反应性B细胞的频率,这些B细胞可识别Delta、Omicron及2002年大流行株SARS-CoV的RBD。通过多色RBD四聚体和单细胞B细胞受体测序,我们证明了广度的产生通过两种不同途径实现。发散的疫苗优先富集克隆上不同的交叉反应性B细胞(不存在于非交叉反应性B细胞库中),其体细胞超突变水平较低,与胚系偏向前体的选择一致。相比之下,匹配的对照疫苗主要在现有克隆系内产生交叉反应性(交叉反应性与非交叉反应性细胞间存在克隆重叠),且突变负担更高,与亲和力成熟驱动的广度获取一致。本研究建立了一种简单的模块化抗原设计原理,即在单一支架上并置适当发散的抗原可促进bnAb倾向B细胞的富集。

papers.abstract: Introduction: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) shows continuous genetic variation, resulting in the emergence of multiple viral lineages worldwide. These mutations can influence viral transmissibility, pathogenic potential, and immune escape, resulting in changed disease pattern. Genomic surveillance allows systematic tracking of viral evolution and circulating variants; thus, monitoring is essential for informed public health planning and clinical preparedness. Aim: To detect the emergence of variants of Omicron lineage in the hilly state of Himachal Pradesh, India. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Medical College, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, India from January 2024 to June 2024. All the SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct value ≤30 received across the state from the four Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) of the state were included. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) extraction was performed using the Q-Line Molecular Viral RNA Extraction Kit, and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) was carried out on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform. Consensus sequences were generated using Medaka and Nanopolish for variant identification and phylogenetic analysis. All demographic and clinical data, like age, sex, clinical presentation, and vaccination status, were recorded and tabulated in Microsoft Excel 2021. The study focused on genomic sequences generated, and the data were presented as numbers and percentages. Results: A total of 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were received. Among SARS-CoV-2 positive cases, adult females constituted the highest proportion, 17 (56.7%), with most patients aged 19-60 years, 17 (56.7%), and the majority of samples originating from Shimla, 11 (36.7%). The study identified JN.1 sublineages in 19 (63.3%) as the predominant cause of infection. Most cases, 20 (66.7%) reported to the outpatient department. Mild symptoms such as fever and cough were seen in 7 (35%) cases. Even though 23 (76.7%) of cases were vaccinated with the COVID-19 vaccine, 10 (33.3%) required admissions. However, no mortality was reported. Conclusion: Tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants revealed the predominance of the JN.1 sublineage of Omicron with generally mild symptoms. Continuous genetic evolution of SARS CoV-2 highlights the need for robust, ongoing genomic surveillance integrated with epidemiological data to enable early detection of emerging variants and strengthen control strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Continuous genetic variation in SARS-CoV-2 drives the emergence of new lineages with potential impacts on transmissibility, pathogenicity, and immune escape, creating a need to monitor circulating variants for public health planning. The study aimed to detect the emergence of Omicron lineage subvariants in Himachal Pradesh, India, addressing gaps in local genomic surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study was conducted at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Medical College, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, India, from January 2024 to June 2024. All SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct value ≤30 received from the state’s four Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories were included.
analysis.methods: RNA extraction was performed using the Q-Line Molecular Viral RNA Extraction Kit, and whole genome sequencing was carried out on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform. Consensus sequences were generated using Medaka and Nanopolish for variant identification and phylogenetic analysis.
analysis.main_results: A total of 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were received, with adult females comprising 56.7% (17/30) and most patients aged 19–60 years (56.7%, 17/30). Samples were predominantly from Shimla (36.7%, 11/30), and JN.1 sublineages were identified in 63.3% (19/30) of cases. Most cases (66.7%, 20/30) presented to outpatient departments, with mild symptoms such as fever and cough in 35% (7/20). Although 76.7% (23/30) were vaccinated, 33.3% (10/30) required admission, and no mortality was reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The predominance of the JN.1 sublineage among sequenced cases indicates ongoing local circulation of Omicron subvariants with generally mild clinical presentation. The study highlights the utility of genomic surveillance in detecting emerging variants within a regional setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the integration of genomic surveillance with epidemiological data to enable early detection of emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants and strengthen local control strategies in hilly regions. The predominance of JN.1 underscores the need for targeted public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=30) and single-centre design limit generalisability, and reliance on Ct ≤30 may introduce selection bias. The evidence is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and lack of controls for confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study from Himachal Pradesh, India, conducted between January and June 2024, investigated the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariants through genomic surveillance. Among 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct ≤30, adult females and individuals aged 19–60 years were most represented, with samples predominantly from Shimla. Whole genome sequencing on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform identified JN.1 sublineages in 63.3% of cases, with most patients presenting mild symptoms and 66.7% managed as outpatients. Vaccination coverage was high (76.7%), yet 33.3% required admission, and no mortality was observed. The predominance of JN.1 highlights ongoing local circulation of Omicron subvariants with generally mild clinical outcomes. The study underscores the importance of integrating genomic surveillance with epidemiological data to detect emerging variants and inform public health strategies in hilly regions.

papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) shows continuous genetic variation, resulting in the emergence of multiple viral lineages worldwide. These mutations can influence viral transmissibility, pathogenic potential, and immune escape, resulting in changed disease pattern. Genomic surveillance allows systematic tracking of viral evolution and circulating variants; thus, monitoring is essential for informed public health planning and clinical preparedness. Aim: To detect the emergence of variants of Omicron lineage in the hilly state of Himachal Pradesh, India. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted at the Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Medical College, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, India from January 2024 to June 2024. All the SARS-CoV-2 positive samples with Ct value ≤30 received across the state from the four Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) of the state were included. Ribonucleic acid (RNA) extraction was performed using the Q-Line Molecular Viral RNA Extraction Kit, and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) was carried out on the Oxford Nanopore MinION platform. Consensus sequences were generated using Medaka and Nanopolish for variant identification and phylogenetic analysis. All demographic and clinical data, like age, sex, clinical presentation, and vaccination status, were recorded and tabulated in Microsoft Excel 2021. The study focused on genomic sequences generated, and the data were presented as numbers and percentages. Results: A total of 30 SARS-CoV-2 positive samples were received. Among SARS-CoV-2 positive cases, adult females constituted the highest proportion, 17 (56.7%), with most patients aged 19-60 years, 17 (56.7%), and the majority of samples originating from Shimla, 11 (36.7%). The study identified JN.1 sublineages in 19 (63.3%) as the predominant cause of infection. Most cases, 20 (66.7%) reported to the outpatient department. Mild symptoms such as fever and cough were seen in 7 (35%) cases. Even though 23 (76.7%) of cases were vaccinated with the COVID-19 vaccine, 10 (33.3%) required admissions. However, no mortality was reported. Conclusion: Tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants revealed the predominance of the JN.1 sublineage of Omicron with generally mild symptoms. Continuous genetic evolution of SARS CoV-2 highlights the need for robust, ongoing genomic surveillance integrated with epidemiological data to enable early detection of emerging variants and strengthen control strategies.

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 样本量较小(n=30)且为单中心设计,限制了结果的普遍性;依赖Ct值≤30可能引入选择偏倚。由于横断面设计及未控制混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: The Role of Community Health Workers in Increasing Access to Essential Health and Social Services During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
papers.abstract: To describe the health care and social services needs addressed by community health workers (CHWs) through referrals in the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. We performed a descriptive analysis of national performance measure data from 67 CCR recipients from 2021 to 2024 documenting referrals, alongside 2 web-based surveys of 63 program administrators and 689 CHWs in the United States in early 2024. CHWs made 464 158 social and 323 769 health referrals, with 282 596 referrals completed. Referrals included services for food, housing, legal assistance, health insurance, lifestyle interventions, chronic disease management, COVID-19‒related care, and maternal and child health care. Referral success was aided by community resources, CHW knowledge, and networking, and limited by costs, mistrust, language barriers, transportation, and child care challenges. CHWs connect individuals to health care and provide follow-up care and social support. Comprehensive and coordinated health and social services are essential to optimize the referral and service delivery. Public Health Implications. Findings support policies promoting the integration, expansion, and sustainability of the CHW workforce. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S331-S340. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308642).

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the role of community health workers (CHWs) in addressing health and social service needs during the COVID-19 pandemic through the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. Findings advocate for policies that integrate, expand, and sustain the CHW workforce to improve access to essential health and social services during public health crises.

papers.title: The Impact of Setting Characteristics on Community Health Worker Roles and COVID-19 Activities: An Examination of the Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities Program.
papers.abstract: To examine the roles and activities performed by community health workers (CHWs) involved in the national Community Health Workers for COVID Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program and examine differences based on setting characteristics. We used data from a CHW self-report survey (n = 689) conducted February through March 2024 in the United States. We ran a series of ordered logistic regression models to examine the association between setting characteristics (i.e., type of organizational setting, organizational experience with CHWs, and populations of focus) and CHW core roles and COVID-19‒specific activities. A total of 69.2% of CHWs in the analytic sample reported performing all 10 core roles. Organizational experience with CHWs and populations of focus emerged as the most salient predictors of CHW core roles and activities. A substantial proportion of CHWs performed the full range of core roles. Results suggest that CHWs in the CCR program tailored their roles and activities according to the unique factors of the communities in which they worked. Public Health Implications. Programs such as CCR may result in CHWs using a wide range of core roles across multiple settings. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S295-S304. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308660).

papers.title: Evaluating the Potential Influence of Federal COVID-19 Response Funding on the Building and Sustainability of the CHW Workforce.
papers.abstract: To describe the potential influence of Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) funding on community health worker (CHW) hiring, retention, and workforce sustainability. A descriptive analysis of a cross-sectional, web-based survey of directors and coordinators of 63 CCR recipient organizations administered between February and March 2024 was conducted in the United States. Survey questions assessed program funding sources, payment mechanisms for CHW services, and CHW hiring and retention. About 65% of CCR recipients relied solely on CCR funds, whereas others leveraged over $117 million in additional funding, mostly federal, to support CCR program implementation. Of 1359 CHW positions supported by CCR, respondents expected to maintain 749. Recipients planned to use grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement as strategies for retention. Federal funding can contribute meaningfully to sustaining CHW employment across different settings, yet sustainability of this vital public health workforce is not assured. Public Health Implications. The findings underscore the importance of long-term investment via diverse funding sources and building programmatic capacity to strengthen and sustain the CHW workforce. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S321-S330. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308646).

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the influence of federal funding on the sustainability of the community health worker (CHW) workforce in the context of the Community Health Workers for COVID-19 Response and Resilient Communities (CCR) program. A cross-sectional survey of 63 CCR recipient organizations was conducted between February and March 2024, assessing funding sources, payment mechanisms, and CHW hiring and retention. The findings indicate that 65% of recipients relied solely on CCR funds, while others used additional federal funding. Of 1359 CHW positions, 749 were expected to be maintained. Retention strategies included grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement. The review highlights the need for long-term investment and programmatic capacity to ensure CHW workforce sustainability, though federal funding alone may not guarantee it.

A descriptive analysis of a cross-sectional, web-based survey of directors and coordinators of 63 CCR recipient organizations administered between February and March 2024 was conducted in the United States. Survey questions assessed program funding sources, payment mechanisms for CHW services, and CHW hiring and retention. About 65% of CCR recipients relied solely on CCR funds, whereas others leveraged over $117 million in additional funding, mostly federal, to support CCR program implementation. Of 1359 CHW positions supported by CCR, respondents expected to maintain 749. Recipients planned to use grant funding and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reimbursement as strategies for retention. Federal funding can contribute meaningfully to sustaining CHW employment across different settings, yet sustainability of this vital public health workforce is not assured. Public Health Implications. The findings underscore the importance of long-term investment via diverse funding sources and building programmatic capacity to strengthen and sustain the CHW workforce. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S321-S330. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308646).

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究通过在美国开展的一项横断面网络调查,对63个CCR受资助机构的主管与协调员进行了描述性分析,调查时间为2024年2月至3月。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 受资助者计划将拨款资金与医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心报销作为留任策略。研究结果强调了通过多元化资金来源进行长期投资以及提升项目能力建设的重要性,以加强并维持CHW队伍。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 联邦资金可在不同场景下为维持CHW就业做出有意义的贡献,但这一重要公共卫生队伍的可持续性仍未得到保障。公共卫生意义。

papers.title: A Community Health Worker-Led Model of Training and Technical Assistance to Support National Community Health Worker Program Implementation for COVID-19 Response: United States, 2021-2025.
papers.abstract: To assess training and technical assistance (TTA) needs among 67 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention-funded community health worker (CHW) programs in the United States and to assess the reach of a national CHW-led TTA program designed to meet the needs identified. From December 2021 through January 2022, we assessed TTA needs through an online survey and interviews with program staff. We used findings to inform TTA content and delivery. From 2021 through 2025, we collected participation data to assess program reach. Among 59 survey respondents and representatives from 10 organizations, funding recipients identified hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning as priorities for TTA. Based on these findings, we developed webinars, communities of practice, leadership training, and individualized TTA. The program reached all funded recipients and generated 8824 participant encounters, 54.7% of whom were CHWs. Health departments implementing CHW programs demonstrated substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA. Policymakers should prioritize sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to support implementation and long-term sustainability of CHW programs. (Am J Public Health. 2026;116(S4):S314-S320. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308665).

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the training and technical assistance (TTA) needs of community health worker (CHW) programs in the United States during the COVID-19 response, focusing on the implementation and reach of a national CHW-led TTA program to support these programs from 2021 to 2025.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review describes an online survey and interviews conducted from December 2021 through January 2022 to assess TTA needs among 67 CDC-funded CHW programs, using findings to inform TTA content and delivery. Participation data were collected from 2021 through 2025 to assess program reach.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that health departments implementing CHW programs demonstrated substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA, with the program reaching all funded recipients and generating 8824 participant encounters, 54.7% of whom were CHWs.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report heterogeneity in TTA needs across regions, populations, or program types, nor does it address conflicting findings or unresolved mechanisms related to CHW-led TTA effectiveness.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review implies that policymakers should prioritize sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to support the implementation and long-term sustainability of CHW programs, particularly in funding, hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates a national community health worker (CHW)-led training and technical assistance (TTA) program designed to support U.S. CHW programs during the COVID-19 response (2021–2025). Using survey and interview data from December 2021–January 2022, the program identified hiring, program implementation, financial sustainability, and peer learning as key TTA priorities. Based on these findings, the program developed webinars, communities of practice, leadership training, and individualized TTA. By 2025, the program reached all funded recipients, generating 8824 participant encounters, with 54.7% involving CHWs. The review highlights substantial demand for and engagement in CHW-led TTA among health departments, underscoring the need for sustained investment in TTA infrastructure to ensure program implementation and long-term sustainability.

papers.title: Cytokine-Driven Hyperinflammation in Long COVID: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, Complement Dysregulation, and Emerging Immunotherapies-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Long COVID, also known as post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection (PASC), is a multisystem condition characterized by persistent symptoms that continue beyond the acute phase of infection. Growing evidence indicates that sustained immune dysregulation involving cytokine‐mediated inflammation, complement activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and viral antigen persistence contributes to its pathogenesis. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms underlying hyperinflammation in Long COVID, highlights emerging biomarkers, and evaluates evolving immunotherapeutic strategies. Methods A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta‐analyses, cohort studies, mechanistic investigations, and clinical trials examining immune dysregulation, inflammatory biomarkers, complement pathways, and targeted therapies in long COVID. Results Persistent elevation of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin‐6, interleukin‐1β, tumor necrosis factor‐α, interferon‐γ, and interleukin‐17, together with activation of the alternative and lectin complement pathways, contributes to endothelial injury, microvascular thrombosis, neuroinflammation, fibrosis, and multisystem dysfunction. Emerging biomarkers include inflammatory cytokines, complement proteins, endothelial activation markers, coagulation indices, and multi‐omics signatures that may improve disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring. Investigational therapies include cytokine‐targeted biologics, complement inhibitors, Janus kinase inhibitors, mesenchymal stem cell therapy, microbiome‐directed interventions, and precision immunotherapy. Conclusion Long COVID results from complex interactions between persistent inflammation, complement dysregulation, vascular injury, and immune dysfunction. Integrating validated biomarkers with precision immunotherapeutic approaches may improve diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management. However, robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials remain essential to validate these strategies and optimize long‐term clinical outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 长新冠,又称严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染后急性期后遗症(PASC),是一种多系统疾病,其特征是感染急性期后持续存在的症状。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究通过PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science、Embase及Google Scholar数据库检索2020年至2026年间发表的文献。优先纳入系统性综述、荟萃分析、病例报告、机制研究及临床试验,这些研究关注长新冠中的免疫失调、炎症生物标志物、补体通路及靶向治疗。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 持续升高的促炎细胞因子(包括白细胞介素-6、白细胞介素-1β、肿瘤坏死因子-α、干扰素-γ及白细胞介素-17)与替代途径及凝集素途径的补体激活共同导致内皮损伤、微血管血栓形成、神经炎症、纤维化及多系统功能障碍。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 仍需开展大规模前瞻性研究及随机对照临床试验以验证这些策略并优化长期临床结局。

papers.title_zh: 细胞因子驱动的高炎症反应在长新冠中的作用:机制、生物标志物、补体失调及新兴免疫治疗——叙述性综述
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Long COVID, also known as post‐acute sequelae of SARS‐CoV‐2 infection (PASC), is a multisystem condition characterized by persistent symptoms that continue beyond the acute phase of infection. Growing evidence indicates that sustained immune dysregulation involving cytokine‐mediated inflammation, complement activation, endothelial dysfunction, thromboinflammation, and viral antigen persistence contributes to its pathogenesis. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms underlying hyperinflammation in Long COVID, highlights emerging biomarkers, and evaluates evolving immunotherapeutic strategies. Methods A narrative literature search was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta‐analyses, cohort studies, mechanistic investigations, and clinical trials examining immune dysregulation, inflammatory biomarkers, complement pathways, and targeted therapies in long COVID. Results Persistent elevation of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin‐6, interleukin‐1β, tumor necrosis factor‐α, interferon‐γ, and interleukin‐17, together with activation of the alternative and lectin complement pathways, contributes to endothelial injury, microvascular thrombosis, neuroinflammation, fibrosis, and multisystem dysfunction. Emerging biomarkers include inflammatory cytokines, complement proteins, endothelial activation markers, coagulation indices, and multi‐omics signatures that may improve disease stratification and therapeutic monitoring. Investigational therapies include cytokine‐targeted biologics, complement inhibitors, Janus kinase inhibitors, mesenchymal stem cell therapy, microbiome‐directed interventions, and precision immunotherapy. Conclusion Long COVID results from complex interactions between persistent inflammation, complement dysregulation, vascular injury, and immune dysfunction. Integrating validated biomarkers with precision immunotherapeutic approaches may improve diagnosis, risk stratification, and individualized management. However, robust prospective studies and randomized clinical trials remain essential to validate these strategies and optimize long‐term clinical outcomes.

papers.title: US Public School Operations During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic forced the sudden closure of schools and a transition to remote learning across the United States. The suspension of in-person education not only altered the delivery of education for millions of students, but it effectively separated many students from vital services and functions that supported their ability to learn and develop. Given the unique role that schools play in educating children and young adults, as well as providing important nonacademic services, their closures led to disruptions in learning, added familial responsibilities, and reduced access to critical social services for students. The reopening of schools for in-person learning or the continuation of remote learning during a public health emergency requires careful planning and consideration to not only ensure the health and safety of students and staff, but also ensure equitable continuation of education and access to nonacademic services. We conducted a scoping review to identify and characterize the literature related to the implementation and impact of interventions and policies used to operate K-12 public schools in the United States during the first 2 years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Through thematic analysis, we found that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination interventions allowed schools to safely conduct in-person learning during the pandemic. Findings from the literature suggest that there are suitable mitigation measures that allowed for the safe operation of public schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. The effective implementation of these measures required adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review examines how US K-12 public schools were operated during the first two years of the SARS-CoV-2/COVID-19 pandemic, a period that began with sudden closures and a shift to remote learning that disrupted education and access to nonacademic services. Through thematic analysis of the literature on interventions and policies, the authors identified that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination enabled schools to safely conduct in-person learning, demonstrating that suitable mitigation measures permitted continued public school operation. The review emphasizes that effective implementation of these measures depended on adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in, and it underscores the need for careful planning to balance health and safety with equitable educational continuity and access to nonacademic services during future public health emergencies. No specific evidence gaps, controversies or quantitative pooled estimates are reported in the supplied evidence.

papers.title_zh: US Public School Operations During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review.
papers.source_body_en: The COVID-19 pandemic forced the sudden closure of schools and a transition to remote learning across the United States. The suspension of in-person education not only altered the delivery of education for millions of students, but it effectively separated many students from vital services and functions that supported their ability to learn and develop. Given the unique role that schools play in educating children and young adults, as well as providing important nonacademic services, their closures led to disruptions in learning, added familial responsibilities, and reduced access to critical social services for students. The reopening of schools for in-person learning or the continuation of remote learning during a public health emergency requires careful planning and consideration to not only ensure the health and safety of students and staff, but also ensure equitable continuation of education and access to nonacademic services. We conducted a scoping review to identify and characterize the literature related to the implementation and impact of interventions and policies used to operate K-12 public schools in the United States during the first 2 years of the COVID-19 pandemic. Through thematic analysis, we found that masking, ventilation, physical distancing, testing, contact tracing, quarantine and isolation, and vaccination interventions allowed schools to safely conduct in-person learning during the pandemic. Findings from the literature suggest that there are suitable mitigation measures that allowed for the safe operation of public schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. The effective implementation of these measures required adequate resources, leadership commitment, and community buy-in.

papers.title: The influence of hypoxia in predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction on admission in 2 centers in sub-Saharan Africa.
papers.abstract: Kidney dysfunction (KD) and hypoxia on admission are separately associated with COVID-19 mortality. Estimation of GFR using creatinine and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) may be useful for stratification of at-risk populations. We performed a two centers retrospective cohort study of 359 COVID-19 patients aged 18 years or older to explore the impact of admission kidney function and hypoxia in predicting COVID-19 mortality. KD at admission was defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) calculated by CKD EPI < 60 mL /min/1.73 m2 using creatinine and hypoxia as a SpO2 ˂ 90%. Survival (time-to death) curves were built using the Kaplan-Meier methods. Association between mortality, hypoxia and KD was evaluated by multivariate Cox regression models with a significance level of the p-value set at 0.05. There were 152 patients (42.3%) with an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and 208 patients (74.8%) with hypoxia on admission. Overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, rising to 59.7% in patients with eGFR below 60 mL/min and hypoxia (p < 0.001). Survival was lower in the group of patients with a eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and hypoxia (p < 0.001). Predictors of mortality were eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with hypoxia (HR 2.05 [1.01-4.16], p = 0.048), eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 without hypoxia (HR 3.20 [1.73-5.94], p < 0.001) and eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with hypoxia (HR 6.55 [3.63-11.84], p < 0.001). KD on admission and hypoxia are common in COVID-19. Its association with in-hospital mortality should encourage its use in the stratification of patients at risk of death. Influence of hypoxia could suggest a pattern of kidney-lung cross talk.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission, highlighting the need to understand how these factors interact in disease progression.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A two-center retrospective cohort study was conducted involving 359 COVID-19 patients aged 18 years or older, with a focus on those presenting with kidney dysfunction and hypoxia.
analysis.methods: The study used multivariate Cox regression models to evaluate the association between mortality, hypoxia, and kidney dysfunction, with a significance level set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: Overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, increasing to 59.7% in patients with both eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and hypoxia (p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the combination of kidney dysfunction and hypoxia significantly increases mortality risk, indicating a potential pattern of kidney-lung cross talk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results emphasize the importance of incorporating KD and hypoxia into patient stratification strategies for improved risk assessment and management in sub-Saharan Africa.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for confounding factors, but the evidence is strong given the clear statistical associations observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the influence of hypoxia on predicting COVID-19 mortality in patients with kidney dysfunction upon admission in two centers in sub-Saharan Africa. It found that overall in-hospital mortality was 27.6%, rising to 59.7% in patients with both kidney dysfunction and hypoxia. The results suggest a potential pattern of kidney-lung cross talk, highlighting the importance of incorporating these factors into patient stratification strategies for improved risk assessment and management. The study's retrospective design and potential for confounding factors limit its evidence strength, although the observed statistical associations are robust.

papers.title: Immunological imprinting shapes the cross-reactive antibody responses to the KP.2 and LP.8.1 vaccine doses.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 subvariant, a lineage derived from the BA.2 strain, led to the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine update to include KP.2 or related JN.1-lineage spike antigens. We evaluated the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immune responses following a single KP.2 vaccine dose in a longitudinal cohort of 21 individuals up to 6 months. KP.2 vaccination increased spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral WA.1 strain, as well as against the BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2 variants. Power-law modeling estimated half-lives for WA.1- and KP.2-specific IgG responses at 770 and 248 days, respectively. Additionally, the KP.2 dose increased IgG1 and IgG4 subclasses more than IgG2 and IgG3 responses to both spike proteins. Serum-depletion experiments using WA.1 or KP.2 proteins demonstrated that most vaccine-elicited antibodies were cross-reactive. Consequently, KP.2 vaccine-induced antibodies retained broad neutralizing activity against recently circulating Omicron subvariants (BA.2.86, KP.3.1.1, XEC, LP.8.1, LF.7, XFG.3.12, PQ.1, BA.3.2.1, and RE.2). Using a live virus neutralization assay, XFG.3.12 showed the greatest reduction in neutralizing titers relative to KP.2 (4.2-fold). In a small subset, an LP.8.1 vaccine dose increased neutralizing activity against the matched variant while maintaining WA.1 and KP.2 cross-reactivity, but only modestly increased antibodies to divergent variants BA.3.2.1 and RE.2. Ultimately, these data indicate the KP.2 mRNA vaccine generates durable, cross-reactive responses against current Omicron subvariants. However, ongoing spike evolution impacts the neutralization of emerging lineages, highlighting the need for continued viral monitoring and timely vaccine updates. IMPORTANCE: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, raising ongoing concerns about how well updated vaccines protect against emerging variants. This study evaluates antibody responses after a KP.2 spike mRNA vaccine dose. It shows that a single dose induces durable and broadly cross-reactive immunity against both earlier strains and recently circulating Omicron subvariants. Despite this breadth, reduced neutralizing activity against certain emerging variants indicates that ongoing antigenic changes can impact vaccine-induced antibody effectiveness. These findings provide insight into how current vaccines perform over time and highlight the need to track viral evolution and update vaccine antigens to maintain broad protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immune responses following a single KP.2 vaccine dose. The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2.86 subvariant necessitated the 2024-2025 vaccine update to include KP.2 or related JN.1-lineage spike antigens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal cohort study was conducted on 21 individuals to assess antibody responses up to 6 months after receiving a KP.2 vaccine dose. The study focused on evaluating the immune response against the ancestral WA.1 strain and various Omicron subvariants.
analysis.methods: The study used a live virus neutralization assay to measure neutralizing titers. Power-law modeling was applied to estimate the half-lives of IgG responses specific to WA.1 and KP.2. Serum-depletion experiments were also conducted to determine cross-reactivity of vaccine-elicited antibodies.
analysis.main_results: KP.2 vaccination increased spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral WA.1 strain, as well as against the BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2 variants. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that KP.2 vaccine-induced antibodies retained broad neutralizing activity against recently circulating Omicron subvariants, but reduced neutralizing activity against certain emerging variants indicates ongoing antigenic changes can impact vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide insight into how current vaccines perform over time and highlight the need to track viral evolution and update vaccine antigens to maintain broad protection against severe disease, hospitalization, and death.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and the focus on a single vaccine dose. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a longitudinal cohort study and serum-depletion experiments, but the results are directly observed and reported.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune response generated by a single dose of the KP.2 mRNA vaccine in a longitudinal cohort of 21 individuals. It evaluates the magnitude, breadth, and durability of humoral immunity against the ancestral WA.1 strain and various Omicron subvariants, including BA.5, XBB.1.5, and KP.2. The results show that KP.2 vaccination increases spike-specific binding and neutralizing antibodies against these variants, with power-law modeling estimating half-lives for IgG responses at 770 and 248 days for WA.1 and KP.2, respectively. Serum-depletion experiments reveal that most antibodies are cross-reactive, and the study highlights the importance of monitoring viral evolution to maintain vaccine effectiveness. However, the study's small sample size and focus on a single dose limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate.
