papers.title: Editorial: The influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on the incidence of viral coinfection
papers.abstract: Abdullah MY (9) studied the impact of COVID-19 on cytokines and gene polymorphisms in patients with type 1 diabetes. Machine learning analyses identified IL-18, CRP, and IL-6 as key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, with IL-18 being the most important.In long COVID patients, Fricke F et al (10) found downregulation of pro-inflammatory genes in classical monocytes, including IL1β and CXCL2. Their analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity (via SNAI1) and impaired monocyte differentiation (via ATF2), leading them to conclude that circulating monocytes are either immature or exhausted. analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients and found that a significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins implicated in viral replication and immune evasion. Their findings highlight how T cell protective immunity is influenced by both the viral replication cycle and HLA type, affecting TCR affinity and clonotype formation. Furthermore, Wen, Y. (12) et al evaluated the heterogeneity and transcriptomic characteristics of Tregs in COVID-19 patients and concluded that Tregs may be activated through the bystander effect, as evidenced by the analysis of TCR clonotype characteristics. The analysis proposed possible analyses of treatment strategies in SARS-CoV-2infected patients.The response against SARS-CoV-2 infection in the elderly population after 6 months was analyzed by Luo Q. The decline in memory B cells and CD69+ and CD38+ T cells, along with the rise in PD-1+ and CTLA-4+ in CD4+/CD8+ T cells and double-negative B cells, suggests that immune responses to BA.5 infection may diminish more quickly in the elderly. (14) developed an explainable machine learning-based mortality risk stratification for older adults with COVID-19, pinpointing core immunological biomarkers and revealing dose-threshold effects. The model identified 10 key features: basophil percentage, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, D-dimer AST/ALT ratio, cardiac troponin I, standard bicarbonate, age, aspartate transaminase, and oxygen saturation. Those parameters were considered critical for calculating patient survival.Chen L et al. (15) reviewed mitochondrial metabolism in COVID-19, highlighting the need for longterm patient data and addressing analytical limitations. They suggested that nutrients like CoQ10, NAC, and creatine could help restore energy metabolism and reduce oxidative stress. The authors emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration for multi-omics studies of mitochondrial-epigenetic interactions, targeted antioxidants, and optimized nutrient delivery systems.Marandu et al. (16) found that vaccination benefited patient recovery from viral infections. While CD4 cells were impacted only during active infection, changes in B and NK cells were noted in the vaccinated group. Additionally, T cell hyperresponsiveness was seen in patients with severe disease. Fialho, M.J., and colleagues (17) studied the role of neutralizing antibodies against COVID-19 and its variants. They concluded that while COVID-19 vaccination effectively generates protective immunity, challenges remain due to immune evasion by Omicron subvariants and waning immunity. These findings highlight the need for updated booster strategies and sustained public health efforts for full vaccine coverage and long-term protection.Yin, Z. et al (18) analyzed data from large-scale serosurveys and found that median IgG antibody levels declined after 3 months. Higher levels were linked to prior infection and vaccination, while older age was associated with annual decay, especially in adults ≥60 years. The IgG threshold for protection against XBB reinfection was 400 AU/mL, with each additional vaccination reducing reinfection risk by 13-15%.Bansai A (19) emphasized that no single protein can diagnose post-COVID patients; phenotypelinked multi-analyte panels show the most promise. Effective post-COVID research requires standardized case definitions, cross-platform validation, and the integration of coagulation assays and extracellular vesicle profiling to improve tissue signal detection.Cruz-Altamirano, E et al. (20) conducted a pilot proteomic analysis on immune dysregulation in dengue following prior SARS-CoV-2 infection. They concluded that previous SARS-CoV-2 exposure may increase dengue severity through cross-reactive antibodies, shifting the immune response toward Th2 and enhancing viral replication. Furthermore, Parra-González M. ( 21) and colleagues reviewed the interactions between dengue and SARS-CoV-2 and their impact on clinical outcomes. They found that co-infection may worsen inflammation, increase vascular and organ damage, and complicate treatment. However, definitive evidence for antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) remains inconclusive, highlighting the need for further mechanistic research.The proteomic profile analysis of hospitalized HIV-and SARS-CoV-2 coinfected patients was studied by Zhang, X. The proteomic profile highlighted disruptions in immunomodulation, thrombosis, and viral entry pathways in people living with HIV caused by COVID-19. However, a larger trial is needed to ascertain the effect of coinfection on immune response.The assessment of Programmed cell death markers in COVID-19 survivors with and without sepsis was analyzed by Mallapu G et al. The analysis revealed two molecular signatures linked to disease severity. The first signature, showing high levels of secreted programmed cell death markers (IL-1-β, IFN-γ, MHC I-A, MHC II-DRB1), was found in both COVID-19-Sepsis and no Sepsis cohorts. The second signature, containing cellular programmed cell death markers (caspase-1, caspase-3, MLKL, p62/SQSTM1), was specific to the COVID-19-Sepsis cohort. These signatures may serve as biomarkers for disease severity and guide therapeutic interventions in critical care.The relationship between SARS-CoV-2 infection and Streptococcus pneumoniae colonization and disease severity was analyzed by Calvo-Silveira, S., et al. Patients with co-infections have higher co-morbidities and severe clinical presentations. Interestingly, non-pharmacological measures may disrupt the S. pneumoniae dynamics, and COVID vaccination can prevent the possibility of coinfection and decrease disease severity.Currey J et al. (25) studied post-viral sequelae using a mouse model of influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in C57BL/6 mice. They infected the mice with sublethal doses of SARS-CoV-2 (MA30) or influenza A (PR8) and analyzed lung and brain tissues at 14-, 21-, and 28-days post-infection using histological analysis and bulk-RNA sequencing. They were able to establish distinct tissue-specific trajectories of long-term pathology following SARS-CoV-2 and influenza infection and provide a foundation for dissecting the mechanisms of post-viral lung and brain disease.The topic presents a compelling collection of manuscripts that cover several critical aspects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, vaccine evaluation, and coinfection, thereby enabling readers to gain a comprehensive understanding of this intricate phenomenon. Notably, there are various proposals for conducting rational risk analyses regarding disease severity, evaluating the immune response to the virus, and assessing the effects of vaccination. Furthermore, suggestions for therapeutic targets that may prove beneficial for future investigations, including those related to long COVID, have been identified. Despite the pandemic originating over six years ago, several unresolved issues persist, particularly regarding post-infection consequences. Consequently, further research is essential to unravel the complex elements associated with infection and coinfection.

papers.title_original: Editorial: The influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on the incidence of viral coinfection

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID influence the incidence of viral coinfection, highlighting the need to understand the interplay between these conditions and other pathogens.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, focusing on the immune response to SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, including non-structural proteins involved in viral replication and immune evasion.
analysis.methods: Machine learning analyses identified key biomarkers of COVID-19 severity, such as IL-18, CRP, and IL-6, while also examining TCR clonotype characteristics in long COVID patients to assess monocyte function and differentiation.
analysis.main_results: A significant proportion of TCRs targeted epitopes across the SARS-CoV-2 genome, including non-structural proteins, and the analysis suggested reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation, indicating potential immune exhaustion or immaturity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the complex relationship between T cell protective immunity, the viral replication cycle, and HLA type, which influence TCR affinity and clonotype formation in SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that understanding T cell responses and their modulation by viral factors and HLA types could inform strategies for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on hospitalized Omicron patients and the lack of long-term follow-up data, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-COVID on viral coinfection incidence. It highlights the need to understand how these conditions interact with other pathogens and affect immune responses. The study analyzed T cell and TCR data from hospitalized Omicron patients, identifying key biomarkers and suggesting reduced inflammasome activity and impaired monocyte differentiation. These findings emphasize the role of the viral replication cycle and HLA type in shaping TCR affinity and clonotype formation. The results have implications for improving immune responses and managing long-term effects of SARS-CoV-2, though the study's moderate evidence strength is limited by its focus on hospitalized patients and lack of long-term data.

(12) 等评估了 新型冠状病毒感染 患者 Tregs 的异质性和转录组特征,得出 Tregs 可能通过旁观者效应被激活的结论,依据是 TCR 克隆型特征的分析。该分析提出在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染患者中可能的 治疗 策略。Luo Q 对老年人 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染 6 个月后的应答进行分析。记忆 B 细胞以及 CD69+、CD38+ T 细胞下降,同时 CD4+/CD8+ T 细胞和双阴性 B 细胞中 PD-1+、CTLA-4+ 上升,提示老年人对 BA.5 感染的 免疫应答 可能更快减弱。(14) 开发了一种可解释的机器学习基于 死亡率 的老年人风险分层模型,定位核心免疫生物标志物并揭示剂量阈值效应。模型识别出 10 项关键特征:嗜碱细胞比例、C‐反应蛋白、降钙素原、D‐二聚体、AST/ALT 比值、心肌肌钙蛋白 I、标准碳酸氢盐、年龄、天冬氨酸转氨酶和血氧饱和度。这些参数被视为计算患者生存率的关键。Chen L 等 (15) 回顾了 新型冠状病毒感染 中的线粒体代谢,强调需要长期患者数据并指出分析局限性。他们建议 CoQ10、NAC 和肌酸等营养素可帮助恢复能量代谢并降低氧化应激。作者强调跨学科合作在多组学研究线粒体‐表观遗传相互作用、靶向抗氧化剂以及优化营养递送系统中的重要性。Marandu 等 (16) 发现 疫苗接种 有助于患者从病毒感染中恢复。CD4 细胞仅在活动感染期间受影响,疫苗接种组的 B 细胞和 NK 细胞出现变化。此外,重症患者出现 T 细胞过度反应。Fialho,M.J. 等 (17) 研究了针对 新型冠状病毒感染 及其变体的中和抗体作用。他们得出 新型冠状病毒感染 疫苗接种 能有效产生保护性免疫,但因 Omicron 亚变种的免疫逃逸和免疫衰减仍面临挑战。这些发现凸显了更新加强针策略和持续公共卫生努力以实现全面 疫苗 覆盖和长期保护的必要性。Yin,Z. 等 (18) 分析了大规模血清流行调查数据,发现 IgG 中位抗体水平在 3 个月后下降。较高水平与既往感染和 疫苗接种 相关,而年龄增大尤其在 ≥60 岁成人中与年衰减相关。针对 XBB 再感染的 IgG 保护阈值为 400 AU/mL,每增加一次 疫苗接种 可将再感染风险降低 13‐15%。Bansai A (19) 强调单一蛋白无法诊断后 COVID 患者;表型关联的多分析物面板最具前景。有效的后 COVID 研究需要标准化病例定义、跨平台验证以及整合凝血检测和细胞外囊泡分析以提升组织信号检测。Cruz‐Altamirano,E 等 (20) 对先前 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后登革热免疫失调进行试点蛋白质组学分析,得出先前 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 暴露可能通过交叉反应抗体增加登革热严重程度,促使 免疫应答 向 Th2 偏移并增强病毒复制。进一步,Parra‐González M. (21) 及其同事回顾了登革热与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的相互作用及其对临床结局的影响,发现共感染可能加重炎症、增加血管和器官损伤并使 治疗 复杂化。然而,抗体依赖增强 (ADE) 的确凿证据仍不充分,强调需进一步机制研究。Zhang,X. 对住院 HIV 与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 共感染患者的蛋白质组学特征进行研究,结果显示 新型冠状病毒感染 在 HIV 患者中导致免疫调节、血栓形成和病毒进入通路紊乱。但仍需更大规模试验以确定共感染对 免疫应答 的影响。Mallapu G 等分析了 新型冠状病毒感染 幸存者有无败血症的程序性细胞死亡标志物,发现两种与疾病严重程度相关的分子特征。第一种特征表现为分泌型程序性细胞死亡标志物(IL‐1‐β、IFN‐γ、MHC I‐A、MHC II‐DRB1)水平升高,见于 新型冠状病毒感染‐败血症和非败血症 队列研究 患者。第二种特征包含细胞内程序性细胞死亡标志物(caspase‐1、caspase‐3、MLKL、p62/SQSTM1),特异于 新型冠状病毒感染‐败血症 队列研究。这些特征可作为疾病严重程度的生物标志物并指导危重症治疗。Calvo‐Silveira,S 等分析了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染与肺炎链球菌定植及疾病严重程度的关系,发现共感染患者合并症更多、临床表现更重。有趣的是,非药物措施可能扰乱 S. pneumoniae 动态,COVID 疫苗接种 能防止共感染并降低疾病严重性。Currey J 等 (25) 使用 C57BL/6 小鼠模型研究流感与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的后病毒后遗症。他们以亚致死剂量的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 (MA30) 或流感 A (PR8) 感染小鼠,并在感染后第 14、21、28 天对肺和脑组织进行组织学分析和散装 RNA 测序,成功建立了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 与流感感染后长期病理的组织特异性轨迹,为解析后病毒肺脑疾病机制提供了基础。该专题汇集了一系列重要手稿,涵盖 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染、疫苗 评估及共感染的多个关键方面,使读者能够全面了解这一复杂现象。值得注意的是,文中提出了多种关于疾病严重程度风险分析、病毒对 免疫应答 的评估以及 疫苗接种 效应的合理方案。此外,还识别出可能对未来研究有益的治疗靶点,包括与 长新冠 相关的目标。尽管疫情已超过六年,但仍有若干未解问题,尤其是感染后后遗症。因此,进一步研究对于阐明感染与共感染的复杂因素仍势在必行。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染和长新冠如何影响病毒共感染的 发病率,强调需要了解这些情况与其他病原体之间的相互作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了住院 Omicron 患者的 T 细胞和 TCR 数据,重点关注 免疫应答 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体的影响,包括参与病毒复制和免疫逃逸的非结构蛋白。
analysis_zh.main_results: 相当比例的 TCR 针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 基因组 的表位,包括非结构蛋白;分析提示炎症小体活性下降和单核细胞分化受损,表明可能存在免疫耗竭或未成熟。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果凸显了 T 细胞保护性免疫、病毒复制周期和 HLA 类型之间的复杂关系,这些因素共同影响 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染中的 TCR 亲和力和克隆型形成。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,理解 T 细胞应答及其受病毒因素和 HLA 类型调控的机制,可为改进 免疫应答 并管理 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的长期影响提供策略指导。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究局限于住院 Omicron 患者,且缺乏长期随访数据,可能影响结果的普适性。鉴于这些限制,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Extracellular vesicles in COVID-19 and long COVID: Structural mediators of viral persistence and immune dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as pivotal structural mediators of immune dysregulation and viral antigen persistence in long COVID. Rather than passive biological carriers, EVs released during SARS-CoV-2 infection function as highly organized lipid nanostructures that preserve the native conformational integrity of viral proteins, including the spike glycoprotein, thereby facilitating chronic signaling and systemic inflammation. Recent advancements in single-particle analytical techniques, such as cryo-electron tomography and atomic force microscopy, are now overcoming the limitations of bulk analysis, enabling the visualization of EV heterogeneity and the quantitative profiling of their nanomechanical properties. This review synthesizes current insights into how EV-associated viral remnants and host-derived inflammatory cargo propagate neuro-immune crosstalk and vascular injury. We conclude by evaluating the potential of EVs as precision biomarkers and bioengineered therapeutic platforms, emphasizing the need for standardized structural characterization to transition these nanovesicles from physiological mediators to clinical diagnostic and regenerative tools.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) as structural mediators in SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID, focusing on their capacity to preserve viral protein integrity, propagate immune dysregulation, and contribute to chronic inflammation and vascular injury.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review synthesizes current insights into EV-associated viral remnants and host-derived inflammatory cargo, emphasizing their structural and functional contributions to neuro-immune crosstalk and systemic inflammation in COVID-19 and long COVID.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Extracellular vesicles released during SARS-CoV-2 infection function as organized lipid nanostructures that preserve the native conformational integrity of viral proteins, including spike glycoprotein, thereby facilitating chronic signaling and systemic inflammation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that recent advancements in single-particle analytical techniques, such as cryo-electron tomography and atomic force microscopy, are overcoming prior limitations of bulk analysis, enabling visualization of EV heterogeneity and quantitative profiling of nanomechanical properties.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how extracellular vesicles (EVs) act as structured mediators in SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID, preserving viral protein integrity and driving chronic immune activation and vascular injury. It synthesizes evidence on EV-associated viral remnants and host inflammatory cargo, emphasizing their role in neuro-immune crosstalk. The review concludes that EVs, as organized lipid nanostructures, facilitate persistent systemic inflammation by maintaining viral protein conformation. It also notes that emerging single-particle techniques are addressing prior analytical limitations, enabling detailed EV profiling. Finally, it proposes EVs as candidates for precision biomarkers and therapeutic platforms, contingent on standardized structural characterization for clinical translation.

papers.title: Preliminary miRNA profiling of plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Epigenetic regulation can play a dual role in viral infection, acting as part of the host defense, while being hijacked to control viral latency, replication, and persistence. During the COVID-19 pandemic, substantial evidence indicated that different SARS-CoV-2 variants may lead to distinct outcomes by affecting different molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, we assessed miRNA expression using high-throughput microarray technology to simultaneously measure the expression of thousands of miRNAs. We focused on: comparing Delta and Omicron infections with healthy controls; identifying specific miRNAs linked to symptom severity; analyzing miRNA expression across different stages of Delta variant infection; and predicting miRNA target genes and evaluating miRNA-mRNA interactions. We identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed simultaneously in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples. These miRNAs were categorized into distinct functional groups based on their roles in viral infection. We observed an association between the expression of specific miRNAs and virus-induced symptom severity and patients' outcomes in both variants. Furthermore, we examined miRNA expression across the various phases of the Delta variant and identified 38 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed. Finally, mRNA-miRNA interaction analysis revealed PTEN, IGF1R, MYC, and STAT3 as the most interacting genes. CONCLUSION: Profiling thousands of miRNAs in response to different SARS-CoV-2 variants offers new opportunities for diagnosis, prognosis, and therapy. Although comorbidities and pathway cross-talk may influence the obtained results, our findings provide novel insights into the host response to SARS-CoV-2 infection at the epigenetic level.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of miRNA in the host response to SARS-CoV-2 variants, particularly focusing on how different variants may affect molecular pathways, including epigenetic mechanisms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used high-throughput microarray technology to assess miRNA expression in plasma samples from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed high-throughput microarray technology to measure miRNA expression levels and analyzed miRNA-mRNA interactions to identify potential target genes.
analysis.main_results: The study identified 65 miRNAs that were significantly differentially expressed in both SARS-CoV-2 variants compared to healthy samples, and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity in patients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could provide novel insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, highlighting potential biomarkers for disease progression.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies targeting miRNA pathways in SARS-CoV-2 infections, offering potential for improved prognosis and treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on miRNA expression without detailed analysis of comorbidities or pathway cross-talk, and the evidence is based on a single study with a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated miRNA expression in plasma from patients infected with distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron, compared to healthy controls. Using high-throughput microarray technology, the researchers identified 65 miRNAs that were differentially expressed in both variants and observed an association between specific miRNA expression and symptom severity. The findings suggest that miRNA profiling could offer new insights into the host's epigenetic response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially aiding in diagnosis and treatment. However, the study's results are limited by the absence of detailed analysis of comorbidities and pathway interactions, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

papers.title: Changes in patient conceptualization of asthma and asthma self-management at key timepoints across the COVID-19 pandemic: A qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background The COVID‐19 public health emergency had significant impacts on people living with long‐term health conditions. The specific impacts of COVID‐19 on people with asthma across key stages of the pandemic are less certain. This study therefore aimed to explore the experiences of people with asthma across the pandemic as risk levels changed in a retrospective cross‐sectional study. Methods Semi‐structured interviews (N = 20), conducted at one timepoint, asked about experiences covering pre‐COVID, initial outbreak/lockdown, restrictions lifting, key‐stages salient to them (e.g., vaccination) and longer‐term. Data were analysed using thematic‐analysis. Findings There were three themes. ‘Doing my own risk assessment’ was an active process using pre‐existing/acquired knowledge to determine risk and subsequent asthma‐management/COVID‐19 behaviours at all stages. ‘Asthma from background to foreground’ highlighted how asthma that was mostly previously unobtrusive was suddenly a ‘pre‐existing condition’ leading to prolonged stress and anxiety. ‘Place in society’ describes how the participants were included/excluded by society due to safety concerns from the initial outbreak onwards, which was influenced by government, friends, family and neighbours, the media, health care systems and even themselves. Discussion Findings highlight how some people with asthma experienced the pandemic as a threat to mortality, with evidence of both poor and good adjustment to their asthma management, as per the Transdiagnostic model. When there are future rapid changes in contexts affecting long term conditions, government agencies should use the present study's findings to (a) guide decision‐making, (b) inform public health messaging aimed at targeting at‐risk populations and (c) provide support for at‐risk populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and self-managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, as the specific impacts of the pandemic on asthma patients were less certain.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was a retrospective cross-sectional qualitative study involving 20 participants with asthma, examining their experiences across pre-COVID, initial outbreak/lockdown, restrictions lifting, and key stages relevant to them, such as vaccination.
analysis.methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted at one timepoint, and data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify patterns in participants' experiences and conceptualizations of asthma and self-management during the pandemic.
analysis.main_results: Three themes emerged: 'Doing my own risk assessment,' 'Asthma from background to foreground,' and 'Place in society,' highlighting participants' active risk evaluation, heightened awareness of asthma as a pre-existing condition, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety concerns.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the pandemic significantly altered how asthma was perceived and managed, with participants adjusting their behaviors based on evolving risk assessments, as per the Transdiagnostic model.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform public health messaging and support systems for individuals with asthma during future public health emergencies, helping to address their unique needs and concerns.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single timepoint data collection and reliance on self-reported experiences, which may introduce bias. However, the evidence is strong given the thematic analysis of a representative sample of asthma patients.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study investigated how people with asthma conceptualized their condition and managed it during key stages of the COVID-19 pandemic. The research aimed to understand the impact of the pandemic on asthma patients, as the specific effects were uncertain. Using semi-structured interviews with 20 participants, the study identified three themes: active risk assessment, asthma becoming a more prominent concern, and societal inclusion/exclusion based on safety perceptions. The findings highlight how the pandemic influenced asthma management behaviors and mental health, aligning with the Transdiagnostic model. These insights can guide public health strategies for supporting asthma patients during future crises. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and single timepoint collection may limit the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为回顾性横断面定性研究,纳入20名哮喘患者,探索其在疫情前、首次新型冠状病毒感染疫情/封锁期、限制解除期及对其具有重要意义的关键阶段(如新型冠状病毒感染疫情关键事件)的体验。

elements_zh.main_results: 共提炼出三个主题:‘进行自身风险评估’、‘哮喘从背景转为前景’及‘在社会中的位置’。前者体现参与者主动评估风险的过程;第二个主题凸显哮喘作为‘既往存在疾病’的突出感知及随之而来的压力与焦虑;第三个主题描述参与者因安全考量在社会中的接纳或排斥体验。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,疫情显著改变了哮喘的认知与管理方式,参与者基于风险评估动态调整行为,符合跨诊断模型。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究发现可为未来公共卫生紧急事件中哮喘患者的公共卫生信息传播与支持体系提供参考,以满足其特殊需求与关切。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于单一时间点的数据收集及对参与者主观体验的依赖,可能引入偏倚。然而,基于代表性哮喘患者样本的主题分析,证据强度较高。

analysis_zh.main_results: 共提炼出三个主题:‘进行自身风险评估’、‘哮喘从背景转为前景’及‘在社会中的位置’。前者体现参与者主动评估风险的过程;第二个主题凸显哮喘作为‘既往存在疾病’的突出感知及随之而来的压力与焦虑;第三个主题描述参与者因安全考量在社会中的接纳或排斥体验。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,疫情显著改变了哮喘的认知与管理方式,参与者基于风险评估动态调整行为,符合跨诊断模型。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究发现可为未来公共卫生紧急事件中哮喘患者的公共卫生信息传播与支持体系提供参考,以满足其特殊需求与关切。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于单一时间点的数据收集及对参与者主观体验的依赖,可能引入偏倚。然而,基于代表性哮喘患者样本的主题分析,证据强度较高。

papers.title: Refining the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response post-COVID-19.
papers.abstract: With the acute stage of COVID-19 behind us, reflection can inform future preparedness. During the pandemic, behavioural and social sciences often studied human behaviour through the lens of alignment with public health recommendations, implicitly treating concern and compliance as desirable and rational. While understandable, this emphasis was relatively narrow. Uncertainty, uneven risk distribution and competing values could have led to heterogeneous appraisals of risk and intervention benefit, even with the evidence available at the time. We show that engaging with the possibility that people could have been heterogeneously rational can broaden understanding of behaviour during COVID-19. Our aim is not to revisit the legitimacy of the response but to encourage reflection on the role of behavioural and social sciences in knowledge generation and highlight opportunities to examine pandemic salience and risk calibration. We outline research directions to guide the field and strengthen decision-making, trust and adaptability in future crises, promoting short-term compliance and long-term trust.

papers.title_original: Refining the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response post-COVID-19.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, specifically examining how these disciplines have studied human behaviour during the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question is about the breadth and depth of this role, particularly in understanding the variability of human responses to public health interventions. The topic boundary includes SARS-CoV-2, its variants, and related terms such as 'post-COVID condition' and 'long COVID'.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic review methods or meta-analysis. It draws on general observations and interpretations of studies conducted during the pandemic, focusing on the conceptual frameworks used to understand human behaviour. The review does not report specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that the focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations during the pandemic was relatively narrow. It suggests that this approach may have overlooked the complexity of human decision-making, particularly in the context of uncertainty and varying risk perceptions. The authors argue that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can enhance understanding of pandemic-related behaviours.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the narrow focus on compliance with public health recommendations may have led to an oversimplified view of human behaviour. It also identifies a gap in understanding how people perceive and calibrate risks during pandemics, especially in the context of uncertainty and uneven risk distribution. These limitations suggest a need for more nuanced approaches in future research.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review recommends expanding the scope of behavioural and social science research to include a broader range of human responses and decision-making processes. It emphasizes the importance of examining pandemic salience and risk calibration to improve future preparedness, decision-making, and trust in public health measures.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of behavioural and social sciences in pandemic response, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic. It critiques the narrow focus on aligning human behaviour with public health recommendations and highlights the need for a more comprehensive understanding of risk perception and decision-making. The authors suggest that considering heterogeneous rationality among individuals can improve pandemic preparedness and response. They also identify gaps in current research and recommend future directions to enhance trust and adaptability in public health strategies.

papers.title: Factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants, 2023-2025.
papers.abstract: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. analysis.summary_en: This review examines factors associated with vaccination against Seasonal Influenza and SARS-CoV-2 in the UK among FluSurvey participants aged [≥]65 years during the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn-Winter campaigns. It highlights that motivations for influenza vaccination include belonging to a risk group and reducing influenza risk, while barriers include concerns about safety and adverse effects. The study found that individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination and vice versa. Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of receiving a COVID-19 vaccination. The review suggests that these findings may inform strategies to improve vaccination coverage in the population. However, other results were weaker or varied by season, indicating potential evidence gaps.

papers.title_zh: 2023-2025年英国FluSurvey参与者中与疫苗接种季节性流感及严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2相关的因素
papers.source_body_en: Seasonal Influenza and COVID-19 vaccination programmes are critical for reducing morbidity and mortality in older adults, yet uptake remains uneven across populations. We aimed to profile vaccination attitudes and examine predictors of COVID-19/influenza vaccination uptake among a UK participatory surveillance system - FluSurvey. We analysed FluSurvey data from participants aged [≥]65 years who were eligible for both vaccines in the 2023-2024 and 2024-2025 Autumn - Winter seasonal campaigns. Descriptive analyses examined self-reported attitudes to influenza vaccination. Logistic regression examined factors (age, sex, socioeconomic status, education, employment, transport, smoking and chronic conditions) associated with influenza and COVID-19 vaccination uptake in each season, adjusting for confounders. Belonging to a risk group and reducing risk of influenza were frequently reported motivations for influenza vaccination, while building natural immunity and concerns around safety and adverse effects were frequently reported barriers. Individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 were more likely to receive an influenza vaccination (aOR2023-2024=13.90 [9.28-21.17]; aOR2024-2025=8.54 [5.82-12.60]), and vice-versa (aOR2023-2024=13.91 [9.30-21.19]; aOR2024-2025=8.52 [5.81-12.58]). Lower educational attainment was associated with lower odds of COVID-19 vaccination (aOR2023-2024=0.59 [0.45-0.78], aOR2024-2025: 0.56 [0.39-0.79]). Other results were weaker or demonstrated variation by season. Our findings highlight recent attitudes and barriers to influenza and COVID-19 vaccination among the FluSurvey cohort, which may inform approaches to improve vaccination coverage in the population.

papers.title: Estimation of serial intervals and time-varying reproduction numbers across SARS-CoV-2 variants in childcare clusters: symptom onset vs. reporting dates
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory virus transmission in childcare centers is facilitated by dense contact patterns, making accurate estimation of serial intervals (SI) and time-varying reproduction numbers (Rt) essential for outbreak management. Although symptom onset dates are epidemiologically preferred, reporting dates are frequently used in routine surveillance due to operational constraints. Reliance on reporting dates may introduce systematic bias in transmission parameter estimates. This study aimed to evaluate differences in SI and Rt estimates based on symptom onset versus reporting dates in COVID-19 childcare clusters across SARS-CoV-2 variant periods. Methods Nationwide data from the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (January 2020–February 2022) were analyzed. Four genotype-confirmed clusters meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included: one Before Delta, two Delta, and one Omicron cluster, each comprising at least 50 epidemiologically linked cases. Serial intervals were fitted using gamma distributions. Time-varying Rt values were estimated using the EpiEstim package separately based on symptom onset and reporting dates. Results Onset-based mean SI declined from 9.85 days (95% CI: 1.97–23.95) in the Before Delta period to 5.34 days (95% CI: 2.00–10.28) during Omicron. In contrast, reporting-based SI estimates were generally longer, reaching 8.87 days (95% CI: 0.71–27.08) during Omicron. Across all variant periods, reporting-based Rt estimates were consistently lower than onset-based estimates. For example, during the Delta period, mean Rt was 1.90 (95% CI: 0.79–3.76) using onset dates compared with 1.08 (95% CI: 0.41–2.39) using reporting dates. Conclusion The choice of temporal reference substantially affects SI and Rt estimation in childcare clusters. Reliance on reporting dates may underestimate real-time transmission intensity and distort epidemic risk assessment. Prioritizing symptom onset data in surveillance systems may improve the accuracy and timeliness of public health responses in high-risk settings.

papers.title: Prognostic impact of right ventricular dilatation and echocardiography use criteria in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The surge of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 [coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)] infection created unprecedented diagnostic and logistical pressures. Given the established potential for cardiac injury and the critical need to optimize scarce resources, establishing the clinical utility and prognostic value of transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) became imperative. AIM: To evaluate the prognostic predictors and the adherence to appropriate use criteria (AUC) for TTE in a highly affected setting. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study analyzing records from patients with confirmed COVID-19 who underwent TTE. Socio-demographic, biochemical, and echocardiographic parameters were collected. Mortality was the primary outcome. We assessed inter-observer agreement (Kappa statistic) for TTE indications (based on American College of Cardiology Foundation 2011 and American Society of Echocardiography 2020 guidelines) and the determination of clinical impact (a subsequent change in patient management). RESULTS: Total 149 patients were analyzed. Median age was 66 years [interquartile range (IQR): 56-73], median hospital stay was 13 days (IQR: 6-23). Overall and intensive care unit mortality rates were 39.6% and 60%, respectively. Elevated biochemical markers (leukocytes, neutrophils, lactate dehydrogenase, and C-reactive protein) were associated with mortality. Crucially, right ventricular (RV) dilatation and/or strain (P = 0.008) was identified as the sole echocardiographic finding significantly predictive of mortality. Inter-observer agreement for classifying AUC was high (κ ≥ 0.798). Furthermore, TTE prompted a change in clinical management in 79.7% of the cases. CONCLUSION: RV pathology is a potent, quantifiable prognostic indicator. While AUC demonstrated high reliability, the significant and frequent changes in management suggest that the current guidelines may possess inherent limitations when addressing the unique, acute prognostic complexities of severe COVID-19 disease.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RV pathology is a potent, quantifiable prognostic indicator. elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings cautiously inform the importance of incorporating right ventricular assessment in the echocardiographic evaluation of hospitalized COVID-19 patients for improved risk stratification and clinical decision-making.
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于回顾性数据,可能引入偏倚并限制因果关系的确立。由于研究性质为观察性且存在潜在混杂因素,证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Inequalities in mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection for people with severe mental illness during and following vaccination roll-out in England: a retrospective, whole-country linked cohort study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: People with severe mental illness (SMI) had a higher risk of death following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared with people without SMI during the COVID-19 pandemic peak. It is unclear whether this risk reduced in later stages after vaccination roll-out. We aimed to assess all-cause and cause-specific mortality following SARS-CoV-2 infection in people with or without SMI across pandemic stages, using whole-country data, while accounting for sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. METHODS: In this retrospective, whole-country cohort study, we analysed linked electronic health records for all people in England registered to primary care who were alive in November, 2019 (>99% of the population). The study population included people who had COVID-19 between Jan 31, 2020, and June 30, 2023, with information on deaths and vaccination. Data extracted from the NHS England Secure Data Environment provided through the British Heart Foundation Data Science Centre CVD-COVID-UK-COVID-IMPACT Consortium linked datasets were curated to form a dataset in July, 2024. Cox regression estimated differences in all-cause and COVID-19 mortality. Analyses were stratified by pandemic stages, defined by WHO policy and UK Government vaccination roll-out: Jan 31-Sept 30, 2020 (stage 1); Oct 1, 2020-July 18, 2021 (stage 2, vaccination roll-out); and July 19, 2021-June 30, 2023 (stage 3, post-vaccination roll-out). SMI comprised schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder, or other affective and non-affective disorder with psychosis. A patient and public involvement panel was consulted during design phases of the study. FINDINGS: 13 463 945 people with COVID-19 were identified, of whom 160 190 (1·19%) had SMI. People with SMI were older [mean age [SD], SMI 49·7 years [17·9], non-SMI 45·0 years [17·6]), had a similar sex split (females SMI vs non-SMI: 56·3% vs 56·6%); and were mostly White British (77·3% or 76·3%). People with SMI had higher all-cause mortality than those without (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1·56, 95% CI 1·53-1·59). All-cause mortality risk in people with SMI was elevated in stage 1 (aHR 1·27, 95% CI 1·22-1·32), but larger in the stage 2 (aHR 1·56, 1·51-1·61) and stage 3 (aHR 1·55, 1·50-1·59). Vaccination prevalence was initially higher for people with SMI (in stage 2: 112 795 [73·2%, 95% CI 72·9-73·4], compared with people without SMI, 8 852 970 [67·4%, 67·3-67·4]). By study end, fewer people with SMI were fully vaccinated (127 145 [79·4%, 79·2-79·6]), compared with people without SMI (11 605 915 [87·2%, 87·2-87·3]. Higher COVID-19 mortality risk in people with SMI persisted but was partially attenuated by vaccination (aHR 1·25, 1·17-1·34). INTERPRETATION: Excess mortality in people with SMI persisted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. Preventive public health and clinical strategies are needed to address excess mortality and lower vaccination. FUNDING: Health Foundation-Academy of Medical Sciences.

papers.title: Sources of Stress in Relation to Sleep Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the National Couples' Health and Time Study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE To assess associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married/cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS We analyzed the National Couples' Health and Time Study, an online survey completed 2020-2021. Stressors were categorized into five domains--1) COVID-19 infection; 2) resources/insurance; 3) overall health; 4) job/income; and 5) public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration (<7 and 7-9) were measured. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and Accepted manuscript ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT95% CIs were obtained from survey-weighted logistic regression models by estimating predicted marginal probabilities. RESULTS Among 3,642 individuals, 46.6% were aged 35-50 years and 44.1% were college graduates. Within racial and/or ethnic groups, the weighted prevalence of overall health stress was 62.0% among Latino and 55.8% among White individuals; the weighted prevalence of job/income stress was 64.3% among Black/African American and 57.6% among White individuals; and the weighted prevalence of public health recommendations stress was highest among White individuals (34.1%), compared with Black/African American (28.1%) and Latino (27.8%) individuals. Overall health stress was associated with poor/fair sleep quality (aPR=1.35; 95% CI: 1.14-1.60) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.19; 95% CI: 1.03-1.39). Job/income stress was associated with fair/poor sleep quality (aPR=1.46; 95% CI: 1.24-1.72) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.31; 95% CI: 1.13-1.52). Race-stratified models showed job/income stress significant among Latino and White individuals for both sleep outcomes, and overall health stress among Latino individuals for duration. CONCLUSION Overall health stress and job/income stress were associated with poorer sleep health among married and cohabiting individuals. Futurework is needed on stress-management and sleep health promotion.

source_records.title: Sources of Stress in Relation to Sleep Health During the COVID-19 Pandemic: Findings from the National Couples' Health and Time Study.
source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVE To assess associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married/cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS We analyzed the National Couples' Health and Time Study, an online survey completed 2020-2021. Stressors were categorized into five domains--1) COVID-19 infection; 2) resources/insurance; 3) overall health; 4) job/income; and 5) public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration (<7 and 7-9) were measured. Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and Accepted manuscript ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT95% CIs were obtained from survey-weighted logistic regression models by estimating predicted marginal probabilities. RESULTS Among 3,642 individuals, 46.6% were aged 35-50 years and 44.1% were college graduates. Within racial and/or ethnic groups, the weighted prevalence of overall health stress was 62.0% among Latino and 55.8% among White individuals; the weighted prevalence of job/income stress was 64.3% among Black/African American and 57.6% among White individuals; and the weighted prevalence of public health recommendations stress was highest among White individuals (34.1%), compared with Black/African American (28.1%) and Latino (27.8%) individuals. Overall health stress was associated with poor/fair sleep quality (aPR=1.35; 95% CI: 1.14-1.60) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.19; 95% CI: 1.03-1.39). Job/income stress was associated with fair/poor sleep quality (aPR=1.46; 95% CI: 1.24-1.72) and <7 hours sleep (aPR=1.31; 95% CI: 1.13-1.52). Race-stratified models showed job/income stress significant among Latino and White individuals for both sleep outcomes, and overall health stress among Latino individuals for duration. CONCLUSION Overall health stress and job/income stress were associated with poorer sleep health among married and cohabiting individuals. Futurework is needed on stress-management and sleep health promotion.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the associations between sources of stress and sleep health among married and cohabitating US adults during the COVID-19 pandemic. Using data from the National Couples' Health and Time Study, stressors were categorized into five domains, including overall health, job/income, and public health recommendations. Sleep quality and duration were measured, and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using survey-weighted logistic regression models. The results showed that overall health stress and job/income stress were linked to poorer sleep health, with notable differences across racial and ethnic groups. The authors concluded that these stressors significantly impacted sleep outcomes, suggesting the need for targeted interventions. However, the study's reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a specific population limit the generalizability of the findings, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: African Americans' perspective on COVID-19 and influenza vaccines: A qualitative study.
papers.abstract: Purpose Annual vaccinations, such as influenza and COVID-19, are a safe and effective way of preventing disease and promoting healthier communities, yet many factors impact uptake. Black and African Americans face numerous barriers to vaccination, reflected in consistently lower vaccination rates and higher hospitalization and mortality rates. This qualitative study aimed to understand perceptions and factors influencing COVID-19 and influenza vaccination among Black and African American adults to inform interventions and outreach to prevent increased acuity of vaccination disparities. Eighty-six Black and African Americans in Milwaukee, WI were purposively recruited to participate in in-depth interviews. Major Findings We identified two themes and five subthemes reflecting vaccine perspectives, influences, and decision-making. In the first theme, similarities and differences in attitudes and willingness to get vaccinated against influenza and COVID-19, we identified three subthemes: (1) prevention was a motivating factor for getting both COVID-19 and influenza vaccines; (2) mistrust surrounding COVID-19 and the COVID-19 vaccine fueled hesitancy; and (3) some participants held discordant beliefs surrounding vaccines and healthcare. In the second theme, sources of vaccine information influencing vaccine perspectives , we identified two subthemes: (1) main sources of vaccine information were television news and the internet, not trusted healthcare professionals, and (2) life experiences affected perspectives. Conclusions Our findings show that vaccine perspectives are shaped by a complex interplay of personal beliefs, experiences, cultural identity, and trust. Public health strategies to improve vaccination rates should acknowledge mistrust, dispel myths and misinformation, and engage trusted communities and messengers across both healthcare and community settings.

papers.title: Data-Driven Change-Point SEIR Modeling of the 2025 COVID-19 Epidemic Wave in China: Model Comparison, Robustness Analysis, and Residual Diagnostics
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: National COVID-19 surveillance in China showed a pronounced epidemic wave during spring 2025, followed by a sustained decline through the summer. This study examined whether that trajectory could be adequately represented by a standard SEIR model with a constant transmission rate or whether the data supported a structural change in transmission intensity. Methods: We analyzed 153 consecutive days of nationally reported COVID-19 cases from 1 May through 30 September 2025. Daily observations were digitized from official China CDC figures and calibrated to the corresponding monthly totals. A standard susceptible-exposed-infectious-removed (SEIR) model was fitted under two specifications: a constant-beta baseline and a piecewise-beta model with a change point selected by profiling candidate dates and minimizing the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The main analysis fixed the latent period at 3 days, the infectious period at 5 days, and used an observation scaling factor q to connect model incidence with reported cases. Model performance was assessed using R-squared, RMSE, AIC, and BIC. Robustness was evaluated through change-point, observation-scale, and biological-parameter sensitivity analyses, followed by residual diagnostics for day-of-week structure and temporal autocorrelation. Results: The AIC profile selected 24 May 2025 as the optimal change point, two days before the observed case peak on 26 May. The piecewise model substantially outperformed the constant-beta model (R-squared 0.8690 vs. 0.6689; RMSE 1,861.07 vs. 2,959.03; AIC 2,313.85 vs. 2,451.74; BIC 2,329.00 vs. The model-implied reproduction index declined from 1.4006 before the change point to 0.8725 afterward. This directional transition from expansion to contraction was preserved across all tested change-point dates, observation-scale values, and nine latent/infectious-period combinations, although goodness of fit deteriorated under some extreme biological assumptions. Residuals retained a strong weekly reporting pattern and positive autocorrelation. Conclusions: A data-driven piecewise transmission rate provided a markedly better description of the 2025 epidemic wave than a constant-rate SEIR model. papers.title: COVID-19 Living Systematic Review Trials
papers.abstract: Explore COVID-19 global registered trials in a frequently updated, open-access, visual database based on IDDO�s living systematic review and developed in collaboration with the COVID-19 Clinical Research Coalition.�This tool aims to help researchers identify current ongoing trials, spot knowledge gaps to explore in future studies, and avoid duplication.Since the COVID-19 outbreak was identified in December 2019, a strong response from the research community has resulted in many independent trials assessing therapeutics, diagnostic tools, vaccines and many other areas. The sheer quantity of ongoing research in this field can make it difficult to assimilate and evaluate. Traditional systematic reviews tend to be a snapshot of a situation and can date quite quickly. Uniquely, here IDDO focuses more widely on a whole research landscape using a living systematic review approach to identify knowledge gaps and inform future analyses. The visualisation tool is frequently updated to ensure the constant tracking of studies with a focus on therapeutic interventions. It: Enables users to pull together and access information on global COVID-19 trials;� Details the study design, sample size, trial phase, and the active pharmaceutical ingredients (API) administered in the studies, where the study was conducted, and whether individual patient data (IPD) will be shared; and Is updated via a quarterly search and standardisation of the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP). The tool showcases the metadata available using three different types of visualisations: geography, lists and analytics incorporating descriptive statistical information. Filter and search options pinpoint research according to selected variables and studies of interest. Researchers have the option to compare studies within the tool and data can also be exported for subsequent analysis. As highlighted in our earlier analysis and its�protocol, innovative tools like these are key to preventing unnecessary duplication of independent research efforts. This work is supported by the�COVID-19 Clinical Research Coalition. IDDO is a�founding member of the Coalition which was�formed to build collaborative solutions and accelerate urgent research on prevention and diagnosis�of COVID-19 in resource-limited settings. It provides�free access to COVID-19 clinical trial protocols. A number of Coalition�working groups�are identifying and addressing the most pressing scientific and operational research questions for resource-limited settings.

papers.title_original: COVID-19 Living Systematic Review Trials

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, and its variants, aiming to explore global registered trials in a frequently updated, open-access, visual database. The central question is to identify ongoing research, spot knowledge gaps, and avoid duplication of efforts in assessing therapeutics, diagnostic tools, vaccines, and other areas related to SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review utilizes a living systematic review approach, developed in collaboration with the COVID-19 Clinical Research Coalition, to track ongoing studies. It is updated quarterly via the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) and includes metadata such as study design, sample size, trial phase, and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights the importance of a living systematic review in capturing the dynamic nature of SARS-CoV-2 research. It provides a visualisation tool that enables researchers to access global trial data, compare studies, and export data for further analysis, ensuring up-to-date and comprehensive tracking of therapeutic interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review acknowledges the difficulty in assimilating and evaluating the sheer quantity of ongoing research. It notes that traditional systematic reviews are static and can quickly become outdated, which underscores the need for a living review approach. However, it does not address specific controversies or evidence gaps in the efficacy or safety of interventions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for innovative tools to prevent unnecessary duplication of research efforts. It also highlights the importance of collaborative solutions to accelerate urgent research on prevention and diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 in resource-limited settings.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the global landscape of SARS-CoV-2 clinical trials through a living systematic review approach, developed in collaboration with the COVID-19 Clinical Research Coalition. It provides a dynamic, open-access database with visual tools to track ongoing studies, identify knowledge gaps, and avoid duplication. The review highlights the value of such tools in accelerating research on prevention and diagnosis, particularly in resource-limited settings. It underscores the need for continuous updates and collaboration to address the evolving nature of SARS-CoV-2 research.

papers.title: Increased risk of pulmonary embolism following SARS-CoV-2 activity in Ontario, Canada
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: SARS-CoV-2 infection is an established prothrombotic trigger, yet the population-level temporal relationship between circulating viral activity and pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate the short-term association between respiratory viral activity and PE, accounting for specific temporal lags. STUDY DESIGN: Ecological time-series study. METHODS: We conducted a population-level time-series analysis of incident PE hospitalizations in Ontario, Canada, from 2011 to 2024. Using distributed lag non-linear models, we assessed associations between standardized weekly activity of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and PE risk over a 5-week lag. RR per SD increase in viral activity were estimated via negative binomial regression with cross-basis terms, capturing exposure-response and lag-response non-linearities, and adjusted for Fourier seasonal terms and secular trends. A single-virus model assessed SARS-CoV-2 alone, while a multi-pathogen model additionally adjusted for influenza A and RSV. RESULTS: Among 70,599 PE cases, SARS-CoV-2 activity demonstrated a significant temporal association with PE. Cumulative RR increased 12% per SD over five weeks (RR 1.12; 95% CI 1.00-1.25). The risk followed a distinct delay trajectory, with weekly cumulative RRs peaking at week 3 (RR 1.22; 95% CI 1.04-1.43). The multi-pathogen model, SARS-CoV-2 showed a higher cumulative RR of 1.26 (95% CI 1.11-1.44), with a lower, non-significant peak at week 3 (RR 1.13; 95% CI 0.96-1.32). CONCLUSIONS: Increased population-level SARS-CoV-2 activity is associated with a heightened risk of PE, peaking at approximately the third week. This delayed peak suggests a protracted thrombo-inflammatory window, likely driven by sustained endothelial injury. These findings highlight the vascular burden of COVID-19 and suggest that infection prevention measures, including vaccination, may provide significant downstream protection against thromboembolic disease.

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: SARS-CoV-2 infection is an established prothrombotic trigger, yet the population-level temporal relationship between circulating viral activity and pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate the short-term association between respiratory viral activity and PE, accounting for specific temporal lags. STUDY DESIGN: Ecological time-series study. METHODS: We conducted a population-level time-series analysis of incident PE hospitalizations in Ontario, Canada, from 2011 to 2024. Using distributed lag non-linear models, we assessed associations between standardized weekly activity of SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and PE risk over a 5-week lag. RR per SD increase in viral activity were estimated via negative binomial regression with cross-basis terms, capturing exposure-response and lag-response non-linearities, and adjusted for Fourier seasonal terms and secular trends. A single-virus model assessed SARS-CoV-2 alone, while a multi-pathogen model additionally adjusted for influenza A and RSV. RESULTS: Among 70,599 PE cases, SARS-CoV-2 activity demonstrated a significant temporal association with PE. Cumulative RR increased 12% per SD over five weeks (RR 1.12; 95% CI 1.00-1.25). The risk followed a distinct delay trajectory, with weekly cumulative RRs peaking at week 3 (RR 1.22; 95% CI 1.04-1.43). The multi-pathogen model, SARS-CoV-2 showed a higher cumulative RR of 1.26 (95% CI 1.11-1.44), with a lower, non-significant peak at week 3 (RR 1.13; 95% CI 0.96-1.32). CONCLUSIONS: Increased population-level SARS-CoV-2 activity is associated with a heightened risk of PE, peaking at approximately the third week. This delayed peak suggests a protracted thrombo-inflammatory window, likely driven by sustained endothelial injury. These findings highlight the vascular burden of COVID-19 and suggest that infection prevention measures, including vaccination, may provide significant downstream protection against thromboembolic disease.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Review on Cardioprotective Biological Properties of Crataegus orientalis in Post-COVID-19 Pandemic Cardiovascular Disorders.
papers.abstract: The growing use of herbal medicinal plants like hawthorn is recognized globally as a way to meet the demand for new natural pharmaceuticals with health benefits. The current review provides a comprehensive overview of the phytochemical constituents and heart-protective therapeutic properties of Crataegus orientalis. Despite numerous reviews on the biological properties of the Crataegus genus. orientalis has emerged as a promising therapeutic agent in managing the increasing cardiovascular complications that have followed the COVID-19 pandemic. This review highlights the primary cardioprotective biological effects of C. orientalis, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, hypolipidemic, antihyperglycemic, antihypertensive, anticoagulant, anti-ischemic, diuretic, and cardiotonic properties, supported by numerous scientific studies in Web of Science, Google Scholar, and PubMed. This updated review provides an overview of the bioactive molecular components of C. orientalis and their cardioprotective mechanisms in cardiac muscle cell biology following the post-COVID-19 Pandemic, exploring its potential as an innovative functional food dietary supplement to enhance plant-derived cardioprotective formulations and its possible health benefits. This study presents a significant challenge for analyzing the active constituents of C. orientalis, which require further research, as they are expected to be promising candidates for developing new approaches to prevent and treat various post-pandemic cardiovascular diseases (CVD).

papers.title: A Three-Domain Framework for Interpreting Publicly Reported Outbreak Surveillance Data: Illustrative Lessons from COVID-19 Outbreaks in China
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Publicly reported outbreak surveillance data are subject to multiple sources of uncertainty, including variation in case ascertainment, testing protocols, and health-system conditions. Standard epidemiological methods can be applied to assess whether reported figures are internally interpretable under reasonable statistical assumptions. This study uses two COVID-19 outbreaks in China—the 2020 Wuhan epidemic and the 2021 Putian Delta-variant outbreak—as illustrative cases to examine methodological considerations in the analysis of publicly reported outbreak data. Methods Three analytical domains were examined using publicly available data. First, reported case fatality rates (CFRs) from Wuhan and the rest of China were compared to illustrate the effect of differential case ascertainment on regional CFR ratios. Second, the RT-PCR testing sequence of the Putian index case was assessed using a temporal plausibility framework informed by published time-varying sensitivity curves, without formal probability estimation. analysis.summary_en: This study presents a three-domain framework for interpreting publicly reported outbreak surveillance data, using two illustrative cases of COVID-19 outbreaks in China. The first domain compared case fatality rates (CFRs) between Wuhan and other regions, highlighting the impact of differential case ascertainment. The second domain assessed the RT-PCR testing sequence of the Putian index case using a temporal plausibility framework, suggesting late-quarantine infection. The third domain compared infection outcomes in two student swab-collector cohorts, emphasizing the importance of person-time standardization for valid comparisons. The analyses underscore methodological principles for interpreting outbreak data, including adjustment for ascertainment conditions, use of time-varying sensitivity assumptions, and standardization for cohort comparisons. The study's findings have implications for improving the accuracy and interpretation of surveillance data, but the reliance on abstract-level data and assumptions limits the confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title: Heritable transgenic schistosomes as a living platform for SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody secretion.
papers.abstract: We report the generation and propagation of not only the first heritable transgenic schistosome line but also a line that secretes a functional therapeutic protein in vivo. Using multiplexed CRISPR/Cas-mediated homology-directed knock-in targeted to a predicted genomic safe-harbor, we inserted a VHH–IgG1 Fc (termed C5-Fc) transgene into Schistosoma mansoni eggs. Single-miracidium infections of Biomphalaria glabrata yielded parental P0 lines; serial passage through snail and mouse hosts produced an F2 cohort in which all parasites carried the C5-Fc transgene and secreted C5-Fc into the murine venous circulation. Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion. Sera from mice harboring C5-Fc transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro with potent activity consistent with the expected ACE2-binding blockade by the C5 variable domain of heavy-chain-only antibody (VHH). These results demonstrate (i) stable, heritable transgenesis of a platyhelminth, (ii) delivery of a biologically active antibody fragment by a live helminth in a mammalian host, and (iii) feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes as sustained, single-dose protein delivery platforms. This technology and delivery system enable new experimental approaches for schistosome biology and motivate exploration of living-foundry therapeutics. A heritable CRISPR knock-in in Schistosoma mansonigenerated a transgenic line that secreted a functional anti–SARS-CoV-2 antibody into mouse circulation. Virus neutralization by infected mouse sera demonstrated a worm-based living biofoundry for sustained, in vivo biologic delivery.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to develop a novel approach for delivering therapeutic proteins, specifically SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies, using transgenic schistosomes as a living platform.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved generating and propagating a heritable transgenic schistosome line that secretes a functional therapeutic protein, using single-miracidium infections of Biomphalaria glabrata and serial passage through snail and mouse hosts to produce an F2 cohort.
analysis.methods: A multiplexed CRISPR/Cas-mediated homology-directed knock-in was used to insert a VHH–IgG1 Fc transgene into Schistosoma mansoni eggs, and molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion.
analysis.main_results: Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission and systemic secretion of the C5-Fc transgene, and sera from mice harboring C5-Fc transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro with potent activity.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate the feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes as sustained, single-dose protein delivery platforms for therapeutic applications, including SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest a potential new strategy for sustained in vivo delivery of biologically active antibodies, which could have implications for the development of novel therapeutic approaches against SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the results are based on in vitro neutralization assays, which may not fully reflect in vivo efficacy or long-term stability of the transgenic platform.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a novel approach to delivering therapeutic proteins, specifically SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies, using transgenic schistosomes as a living platform. Researchers generated a heritable transgenic line of Schistosoma mansoni that secretes a functional antibody fragment into the murine venous circulation. Molecular assays confirmed chromosomal insertion, germline transmission, and systemic secretion of the transgene. Sera from mice with these transgenic worms neutralized SARS-CoV-2 in vitro, demonstrating the feasibility of using transgenic schistosomes for sustained, single-dose protein delivery. The findings suggest potential applications in developing new therapeutic strategies against SARS-CoV-2. However, the study is based on abstract-only evidence and relies on in vitro results, which may not fully capture in vivo efficacy or long-term stability. The results highlight the possibility of using live helminths as biologic delivery systems, opening new avenues for research and therapeutic development.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一种新型递送治疗蛋白(特指严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体)的方法,利用转基因血吸虫作为活体平台。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究通过单毛蚴感染双脐螺并经螺类与小鼠宿主连续传代,生成并传代携带可遗传转基因的血吸虫株系,最终获得F2 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 研究采用多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将VHH–IgG1 Fc转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵;分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。
elements_zh.main_results: 分子检测确认C5-Fc转基因的染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌;携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外以强效活性中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断一致。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明转基因血吸虫可作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台用于治疗应用(包括严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体),展现了该技术的可行性与创新性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提示了一种潜在的新策略,用于持续体内递送生物活性抗体,可能对开发针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及相关病毒的新型治疗方法产生影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究仅基于摘要证据,结果依赖体外中和实验,可能无法完全反映体内疗效或转基因平台的长期稳定性。

papers.abstract_zh: 本研究报道了首个可遗传转基因血吸虫株系的生成与传代,以及体内分泌功能性治疗蛋白的株系。研究通过多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将靶向预测基因组安全港的VHH–IgG1 Fc(命名为C5-Fc)转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵。单毛蚴感染双脐螺后获得亲代P0株系;通过螺类与小鼠宿主的连续传代,获得F2 队列研究,其中所有寄生虫均携带C5-Fc转基因并将C5-Fc分泌至小鼠静脉循环。分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断(由重链单域抗体C5可变区介导)一致。研究结果证明:(1)扁形动物稳定可遗传转基因,(2)活体蠕虫在哺乳动物宿主中递送生物活性抗体片段,(3)转基因血吸虫作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台的可行性。该技术与递送系统为血吸虫生物学研究提供新的实验方法,并为活体生物制药探索提供动力。曼氏血吸虫的可遗传CRISPR整合产生了一个分泌功能性抗严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2抗体进入小鼠循环的转基因株系。感染小鼠血清的病毒中和实验证明了基于蠕虫的活体生物工厂,可实现持续体内生物制剂递送。
papers.summary_zh: 本研究报道了首个可遗传转基因血吸虫株系的生成与传代,以及体内分泌功能性治疗蛋白的株系。研究通过多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将靶向预测基因组安全港的VHH–IgG1 Fc(命名为C5-Fc)转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵。单毛蚴感染双脐螺后获得亲代P0株系;通过螺类与小鼠宿主的连续传代,获得F2 队列研究,其中所有寄生虫均携带C5-Fc转基因并将C5-Fc分泌至小鼠静脉循环。分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断(由重链单域抗体C5可变区介导)一致。研究结果证明:(1)扁形动物稳定可遗传转基因,(2)活体蠕虫在哺乳动物宿主中递送生物活性抗体片段,(3)转基因血吸虫作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台的可行性。该技术与递送系统为血吸虫生物学研究提供新的实验方法,并为活体生物制药探索提供动力。曼氏血吸虫的可遗传CRISPR整合产生了一个分泌功能性抗严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2抗体进入小鼠循环的转基因株系。感染小鼠血清的病毒中和实验证明了基于蠕虫的活体生物工厂,可实现持续体内生物制剂递送。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一种新型递送治疗蛋白(特指严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体)的方法,利用转基因血吸虫作为活体平台。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究通过单毛蚴感染双脐螺并经螺类与小鼠宿主连续传代,生成并传代携带可遗传转基因的血吸虫株系,最终获得F2 队列研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究采用多重CRISPR/Cas介导的同源定向整合技术,将VHH–IgG1 Fc转基因插入曼氏血吸虫卵;分子检测确认染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌。
analysis_zh.main_results: 分子检测确认C5-Fc转基因的染色体插入、生殖系传播及系统性分泌;携带C5-Fc转基因蠕虫的小鼠血清在体外以强效活性中和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,其活性与预期的ACE2结合阻断一致。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果证明转基因血吸虫可作为持续单次剂量蛋白递送平台用于治疗应用(包括严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2中和抗体),展现了该技术的可行性与创新性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果提示了一种潜在的新策略,用于持续体内递送生物活性抗体,可能对开发针对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及相关病毒的新型治疗方法产生影响。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究仅基于摘要证据,结果依赖体外中和实验,可能无法完全反映体内疗效或转基因平台的长期稳定性。
